Join a team where your leadership shapes outcomes — not just for the business, but for the people around you.

About the Role
 As the Operations Team Lead for Central Property , you will be at the heart of a dynamic underwriting operation — building a high-performing team, shaping smarter processes, and ensuring every moving part works together seamlessly. Your leadership will directly influence productivity, process efficiency, accuracy, and profitability across multiple underwriting teams. This is a role for someone who leads with purpose, communicates with clarity, and is always looking for better ways to work. If you are energized by the intersection of people leadership and operational strategy, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful mark.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead the property operations team — set a clear direction, foster a high-performance culture, and ensure the team consistently delivers against service standards and business objectives

• Support operational consistency by championing adherence to documented procedures, Standard Operating Procedures, and best practices across all workflows and processes

• Ensure control and audit readiness — maintain robust operational controls, proactively identify risk areas, and ensure the team is always prepared for internal and external audit requirements

• Monitor productivity, quality, and performance — track key metrics, identify trends, address gaps with timely interventions, and celebrate wins that drive continuous improvement

• Serve as a key partner to underwriting and operational stakeholders — build trusted, collaborative relationships across the business to align priorities, resolve issues, and deliver seamless end-to-end outcomes

• Manage and develop team members — invest in the growth of each individual through coaching, constructive feedback, and tailored development plans, while maintaining clear accountability and high service standards

About the Team
 We are a curious, collaborative, and client-focused team that is always seeking innovative ways to tackle complex challenges. From thought leadership and research to creative problem-solving and idea-sharing, we bring energy and enthusiasm to everything we do.
 At our core, we are driven by a commitment to putting clients first — working alongside them to co-create solutions and deliver real, lasting value. As Crisis Management professionals, we combine deep insurance industry knowledge with sharp operational expertise, helping clients navigate complexity with confidence. We are a team that supports one another, celebrates diverse perspectives, and believes that great outcomes are built on trust, collaboration, and a shared commitment to excellence.

About You
 You are an experienced, energetic leader who takes full ownership of outcomes and knows how to bring out the best in people while keeping operations running at their peak. You balance preserving what works with driving meaningful improvements , and you approach every challenge with critical thinking and sound judgment — knowing when to act independently and when to escalate. You are a natural consensus builder who can provide thoughtful pushback to stakeholders when needed, all while maintaining strong, trust-based relationships. You lead with empathy, communicate with clarity, and inspire those around you to do their best work.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in commercial insurance operations, with solid knowledge and understanding of commercial insurance principles and practices

• Insurance industry background is essential, including direct involvement with Commercial Lines products and coverages (university degree or equivalent work experience required)

• Demonstrated leadership experience — proven ability to encourage, empower, develop, and lead a team, providing constructive feedback and fostering a positive, inclusive team culture

• High proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), with the ability to think analytically and demonstrate financial acuity

• Strong organizational and prioritization skills — able to plan, coordinate, and monitor team workloads effectively, even under tight timeframes and shifting priorities

• Accountability and ownership mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, follow through on commitments, and hold yourself and others to a high standard

• Consensus building and team leadership — skilled at aligning diverse perspectives, building buy-in, and driving collective progress toward shared goals

• Autonomy and independent decision-making — comfortable operating with a high degree of independence while exercising strong judgment about when to escalate issues to senior stakeholders

• Critical thinking and balanced judgment — able to evaluate situations objectively, weigh competing priorities, and find the right balance between preserving effective practices and implementing improvements

• Stakeholder management with confidence — able to provide appropriate and constructive pushback to stakeholders while maintaining strong, collaborative service relationships
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Experience working in a matrix or globally distributed environment , collaborating across teams with sensitivity to cultural differences and diverse working styles

• A proactive, self-directed work style with a genuine eagerness to seek out new knowledge, challenge the status quo, and identify opportunities for improvement

• Experience leading process improvement or systems enhancement initiatives , with a track record of delivering tangible operational gains

• Comfort with ambiguity and change , with the ability to adapt quickly and bring others along on the journey

This position is flexible to our Alpharetta, GA, Windsor, CT or Kansas City, MO office, with potential to consider other locations for a qualified individual. Our company uses a hybrid work model requiring at least three days in the office each week, with the option to work onsite full-time if preferred. This position is not eligible for full-time telework, relocation assistance or visa sponsorship.

The estimated base salary range for this position is $76,000 to $126,000. The specific salary offered for this, or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short- and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.

We offer innovative insurance solutions to large and midsized multinational corporations from our approximately 50 locations worldwide. jobs.description:
Are you early in your insurance operations career and interested in working in a global, fast-paced environment? Join Swiss Re Corporate Solutions and support Trade Credit Insurance operations across the transaction lifecycle. As part of a newly established back-end TCI Operations team, you will contribute to accurate processing, reconciliation, and control activities supporting global integration and ongoing operations.
 About the Role
 As TCI Operations Analyst, you will support trade credit insurance operations across key back-end processes, including partner clearance, premium reconciliation, data migration, and cash allocation activities.
 This role reports to the VP, Operations Manager, TCI Integration, and is part of a global Credit & Surety Operations team supporting integration and ongoing operational activities. You will work closely with colleagues across underwriting, finance, and technical accounting to ensure timely and accurate processing in line with applicable Swiss Re Standards.
 Key Responsibilities

• Operational Delivery

• Support trade credit insurance operations across the transaction lifecycle

• Perform partner screening and clearance activities in accordance with established procedures

• Conduct premium reconciliations, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency

• Execute data migration and system-related activities as required for integration and project work

• Handle cash allocation and assist in resolving related discrepancies

• Perform four-eyes checks on selected bookings to ensure control compliance

• Investigate and resolve operational queries in coordination with internal stakeholders

• Maintain accurate documentation and process records in line with applicable Swiss Re Standards

• Audit and Reporting

• Support internal and external audit requirements related to technical accounting and partner clearance

• Prepare ad hoc operational reports as required

 The Credit & Surety Operations team supports global business partners in delivering high-quality, well-governed delegated authority and specialty insurance programs. Working across regions, the team collaborates closely with underwriting, finance, legal, and risk functions to ensure strong operational standards and effective oversight of partner relationships.
 As part of this team, you will work in a collaborative, international environment that values structure, accountability, and continuous improvement.

 You are detail-oriented and take ownership of your day-to-day responsibilities. You are comfortable working with structured processes and understand the importance of accuracy and control in financial and insurance operations.
 You are a collaborative team player who communicates clearly and works effectively with colleagues across functions and regions. You are adaptable and able to manage changing priorities in a dynamic environment. You are proactive, eager to learn, and interested in developing your expertise in trade credit insurance operations.
 Key Requirements

• 3+ years of experience in insurance operations, technical accounting, credit control, or financial services; experience with trade credit insurance or specialty commercial lines ideal but not required

• Basic understanding of insurance operations and accounting processes

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

• Good understanding of administrative and financial control processes

• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

jobs.description:
This is an opportunity to join our Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) Americas team. If you thrive on achieving profitability and growth targets, this role may be the right fit for you? We are looking for someone who can bring leadership skills, loves collaborating with internal and external partners, and has experience leading complex transactional insurance deals!
 About the Role:
 This position is accountable for the performance of the ART Americas business segment based on pre-agreed Key Performance Indicators. The Structurer enables profitable growth by generating and cultivating a strong transaction pipeline in a variety of structured insurance products and solutions.
 Key responsibilities include:

• Source, structure, and sell bespoke solutions jointly with underwriting, customer and broker distribution management for structured insurance products and solutions.

• Drive the formulation, execution and regulatory compliance of the business strategy based on accounting, tax and legal requirements to mitigate reputational risk.

• Consult and structure transactions with risk managers and C-Suite of our corporate customers and brokers.

• Develop and maintain professional relationships with key internal parties and external clients, brokers, risk, and financial managers, including high profile at industry events, media outreach and speaking engagements.

• Meet plan objectives in collaboration with regional customer and broker distribution managers, underwriting teams and internal professional service providers.

• Develop and promote a high-performance environment in which success is dependent on an inclusive team approach, cultivating key works with internal parties, customer and broker distribution managers, underwriting, risk management as well as Swiss Re group support teams such as Operations, Legal, Accounting, Tax and Finance.
 About the Team:
 Driving the innovation in products, solutions, and process, we ensure the ART Americas team is known in the market as a consistent and reliable partner for innovative Parametric Nat Cat solutions. Our team takes pride in growing the portfolio and being an industry leader in the development of new products and solutions!
 About You:
 Do you enjoy working in a multi-cultural and cross-functional environment? Can you bring sound strategic, negotiating, and decision-making skills along with excellent communication acumen? If this sounds like you and you have the following skill sets then we look forward to hearing from you!

• Master's or bachelor's degree preferred in corporate finance, economics, mathematics; or equivalent education

• Minimum of 8 years of experience working in the North American insurance market in underwriting (property, treaty, etc.), risk management or insurance sales/marketing complemented by practical experience in structuring and executing structured insurance solutions

• Solid knowledge of traditional and structured insurance products and markets

• Strong financial acumen with deep capital and financial management proficiency as well as analytical and modelling capabilities

• Strong entrepreneurial mindset and focus on execution, and a pronounced bias towards closing deals

• Excellent collaborator with the ability to work well in a virtual team environment
 **Willingness to travel is required.
 Swiss Re has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office three days per week.

jobs.title: Senior Auditor - P&C Underwriting (Hybrid; 80- 100%)
jobs.description:
Are you a critical thinker who likes to analyze complex topics and provide insights on risks? Do you enjoy working in a diverse team that employs innovative techniques and tools? Join us at Group Internal Audit and help us to advance Swiss Re's resilience.
 About the Role
 As a Senior Auditor with focus on P&C Underwriting in Group Internal Audit (GIA), you will have the opportunity to leverage your underwriting knowledge across the end-to-end value chain while participating in a variety of audit activities. You will engage with senior underwriters and function heads on a regular basis across multiple underwriting lines of business.
 This role is an opportunity to deal with themes that have direct impact on the execution of Swiss Re strategy.
 Ke y Responsibilities:

• Lead / contribute to various audits, using your expertise to deliver technically excellent reports on time.

• Provide management with insights into improvement opportunities, building on audit findings.

• Monitor risk landscape, analyze relevant datapoints to inform GIA risk assessment and audit plans

• Coaching other members of the audit team on technical underwriting topics.

• Challenging the audit teams to excel by acting as a role model.

About the Team
 Group Internal Audit is an international team of Auditors with the vision of 'Advancing Swiss Re's Resilience'. We seek to be problem solvers who lead from every seat, challenge the status quo, understand risk, and demonstrate that we are responsive to risk.
 We apply innovative and risk-focused techniques that ensure that our audit effort is proportionate to risk, and we continuously extend the use of data analytics and automation within our audit processes.
 About You

jobs.description:
About the Role

The Business Services team in Corporate Solutions Operations is looking for an open-minded Underwriting Assistant with a can-do spirit to be based in Singapore. You will be responsible for primarily supporting the Property and Casualty portfolio.

The role involves high interaction and coordination with underwriters and other internal/external departments, both locally and overseas.

Your main responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

• Preparation of policy documentation.

• Setting up and finalizing policies in various systems (underwriting, pricing, invoices etc.) ensuring data accuracy.

• To support the Underwriting team with renewal preparation (deal analysis of renewal account) and endorsement triaging and preparation.

• Handling of closings and contract changes.

• Creating and maintaining records both electronically, if required, following established guidelines and processes.

• Handling basic underwriting tasks, renewals, quotes, endorsements including Broker engagement where required.

• To be in contact with your brokers and customers on a regular basis and attend broker and customer meeting where needed.

• Providing support in premium handling, monitoring, and chasing.

• Collaborating with outsourced providers on queries and issues.

• Development and maintenance of Standard Operating Procedures.

• Modifying, updating, and processing changes in applicable tools, systems, and documents, as needed; and

• Participating in and leading small projects, as required.

About the Team

The team is responsible for administration and operational tasks and support to Underwriters in administration and Underwriting assistance.

About You

• Graduate degree in Business Management or Operations Management

• Passion to deliver excellent service to our customers and internal stakeholders

• Demonstrated analytical skills to determine and communicate recommendations to customers.

• Ability to analyze data following established processes and procedures accurately and efficiently.

• A dedicated team player with ability to demonstrate the highest level of professionalism and integrity.

• Solutions and results oriented individual with an ability to multi-task.

• Strong service and quality mindset.

• Demonstrated intermediate to advanced computer skills and experience with Microsoft Office, Lotus Notes and the Internet. Experience with Visio, Adobe Acrobat Pro, Nitro PDF, MS Project, and Business Objects would be a plus.

• Excellent communication skills – reading, written and verbal

jobs.description:
About the Team

The General Ledger Accounting Services team is responsible for executing group and statutory accounting activities in line with IFRS and local statutory requirements. The team performs period-end closing, ensures the accuracy and completeness of general ledger postings, and delivers timely group and local financial reporting. In addition, the team supports statutory financial statements, audits, regulatory reporting, and collaborates closely with local finance teams and group functions to ensure compliance, transparency, and strong financial controls. As part of the team, you will actively identify opportunities to further develop, streamline, and improve accounting and closing processes, while strengthening collaboration with internal and external partners to enhance overall delivery quality.

About the Role

• Support accounting, reporting, and closing activities for assigned real estate entities and portfolios, including monthly, quarterly, and year-end close processes
 • Ensure accurate, complete, and timely accounting of real estate transactions in accordance with IFRS and internal accounting policies
 • Perform accounting for real estate investments, including construction projects, asset capitalization, depreciation, accruals, and intercompany transactions
 • Perform reconciliations, analyses, and controls to ensure data quality, completeness, and accuracy of financial information
 • Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, profit and loss analyses, and portfolio reporting, providing explanations for significant movements and variances
 • Coordinate with Asset Management, Carrier Management, Project Managers, external service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate financial reporting
 • Execute and document key controls and maintain audit-ready supporting documentation in line with internal and external requirements
 • Support statutory reporting, audits, and regulatory requirements as applicable
 • Take ownership of assigned entities and portfolios and provide complete and accurate deliverables in line with reporting timelines
 • Support process improvements, simplification initiatives, automation efforts, and knowledge sharing within and outside of the team
 • Handle ad hoc accounting, reporting, analysis, and project-related tasks as required

About You

• You have at least five years of work experience in accounting, financial reporting, or real estate accounting
 • You have a university degree in Accounting, Audit, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field
 • Knowledge of IFRS and financial reporting principles; real estate accounting experience is an advantage
 • Strong understanding of accounting controls, reconciliations, and financial reporting processes
 • Experience with SAP or other financial accounting systems
 • Proven IT skills, including MS Office; experience with data analytics, automation tools, Copilot, or ChatGPT is an advantage
 • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
 • Great teammate with strong communication and stakeholder management skills
 • You are proactive, accountable, and motivated to drive continuous improvement
 • Fluent written and spoken English
 This role is a 1-year contract.
 Our company has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office at least three days per week
 For Slovakia the base salary range for this position is between EUR 2,100 and EUR 3,400 per month (for a full-time role).
The specific salary offered considers:
 • the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role,
 • the applicant’s own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialization, skills and experience.
In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for additional rewards and benefits.

We look forward to your application!

The General Ledger Accounting Services team is responsible for executing group and statutory accounting activities in line with IFRS and local statutory requirements. The team performs period-end closing, ensures the accuracy and completeness of general ledger postings, and delivers timely group and local financial reporting. As part of the team, you will actively identify opportunities to further develop, streamline, and improve accounting and closing processes, while strengthening collaboration with internal and external partners to enhance overall delivery quality.

About the Role

• Support accounting, reporting, and closing activities for assigned real estate entities and portfolios, including monthly, quarterly, and year-end close processes
• Ensure accurate, complete, and timely accounting of real estate transactions in accordance with IFRS and internal accounting policies
• Perform accounting for real estate investments, including construction projects, asset capitalization, depreciation, accruals, and intercompany transactions
• Perform reconciliations, analyses, and controls to ensure data quality, completeness, and accuracy of financial information
• Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, profit and loss analyses, and portfolio reporting, providing explanations for significant movements and variances
• Coordinate with Asset Management, Carrier Management, Project Managers, external service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate financial reporting
• Execute and document key controls and maintain audit-ready supporting documentation in line with internal and external requirements
• Support statutory reporting, audits, and regulatory requirements as applicable
• Take ownership of assigned entities and portfolios and provide complete and accurate deliverables in line with reporting timelines
• Support process improvements, simplification initiatives, automation efforts, and knowledge sharing within and outside of the team
• Handle ad hoc accounting, reporting, analysis, and project-related tasks as required

About You

• You have at least five years of work experience in accounting, financial reporting, or real estate accounting
• You have a university degree in Accounting, Audit, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field
• Knowledge of IFRS and financial reporting principles; real estate accounting experience is an advantage
• Strong understanding of accounting controls, reconciliations, and financial reporting processes
• Experience with SAP or other financial accounting systems
• Proven IT skills, including MS Office; experience with data analytics, automation tools, Copilot, or ChatGPT is an advantage
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
• Great teammate with strong communication and stakeholder management skills
• You are proactive, accountable, and motivated to drive continuous improvement
• Fluent written and spoken English
This role is a 1-year contract.
Our company has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office at least three days per week

• the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role,

Locations:
Ciudad de México, Mexico State, MX |
Mexico City, MX

Agriculture Underwriter – Latin America
 About the Role
 Are you ready to take the next step in your agricultural reinsurance career?
 As an Agriculture Underwriter for Latin America, you will contribute to the profitable growth and management of Swiss Re's agriculture reinsurance portfolio across the region. You will combine technical underwriting expertise with strong market engagement, supporting both treaty and facultative business while helping to develop innovative risk transfer solutions for agricultural clients.
 This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of underwriting, portfolio management, analytics, and product development. You will collaborate closely with clients, brokers, and internal experts to deliver data-driven insights, strengthen client relationships, and support Swiss Re's leadership position in agricultural reinsurance across Latin America.
 As part of a geographically distributed team, this role requires a high degree of ownership, initiative, and self-direction. You will be empowered to manage your responsibilities independently, drive projects forward, and proactively identify opportunities to improve portfolio performance, client outcomes, and business growth.

About the Team
 You will join the Agriculture Americas team, a collaborative and highly specialized group within Swiss Re's reinsurance business. The team is responsible for delivering underwriting excellence, portfolio performance, and innovative agricultural risk solutions across diverse markets in the region.
 Working closely with Client Management, Agriculture Product Center and Center of Excellence for Parametric, and other cross-functional teams, you will contribute to sustainable portfolio growth, technical innovation, and the development of tailored solutions for both private and public sector clients.
 As part of Swiss Re's global agriculture community, you will have access to a network of agriculture specialists across the Americas, Europe, and Asia, gaining exposure to advanced modelling capabilities, remote sensing applications, climate analytics, and emerging agricultural technologies.
 Key Responsibilities
 Underwriting & Portfolio Management

• Underwrite and manage a portfolio of Agriculture treaty and facultative business, ensuring sustainable profitability and adherence to Swiss Re underwriting guidelines and best practices

• Evaluate, structure, and price reinsurance solutions through quantitative analysis, portfolio assessment, and sound underwriting judgment

• Support portfolio steering activities, including accumulation management, diversification analysis, structure optimization, and performance monitoring

• Generate portfolio insights and analytics to support underwriting decisions and strategic portfolio management

• Contribute to portfolio reviews, business planning, and performance assessments across the Latin American agriculture portfolio

Client & Market Development

• Build and strengthen relationships with clients, brokers, and key market stakeholders across Mexico and Latin America

• Support business origination efforts by identifying opportunities for profitable growth and differentiated solutions

• Collaborate with Client Managers and underwriting colleagues to deepen client engagement and strengthen Swiss Re's market position

• Support client discussions through technical insights, portfolio analyses, and market intelligence

• Contribute to thought leadership initiatives and promote Swiss Re's agricultural expertise in the market

Innovation & Technical Development

• Support the development of new agricultural insurance and reinsurance solutions, including parametric and data-driven products

• Collaborate with Agriculture R&D and technical experts on modelling initiatives, product design, and solution development

• Apply analytical tools and technologies to improve risk assessment, portfolio monitoring, and product calibration

• Contribute to projects involving remote sensing, geospatial analytics, climate data, and emerging technologies relevant to agricultural risk management

• Help translate technical analyses into practical insights that create value for clients and support business decisions

About You
 You are a well-rounded agricultural insurance or reinsurance professional who combines strong technical capabilities with commercial awareness and relationship-building skills.
 You are naturally curious, highly self-motivated, and comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy. You enjoy solving complex problems, working with data, engaging with clients, and taking ownership of initiatives from concept through execution. You thrive in a collaborative international environment and can effectively prioritize, make decisions, and deliver results with limited day-to-day supervision.

Experience & Background

• Bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Agricultural Economics, Actuarial Science, Natural Sciences, Engineering, Insurance, or a related discipline (Master's degree preferred)

• Relevant experience in agricultural insurance or reinsurance underwriting, product development, portfolio analytics, or related technical roles

• Good understanding of agricultural insurance and reinsurance markets within Latin America

• Experience working with agricultural production systems, crop insurance, livestock insurance, or related risk management solutions

• Experience interacting with clients, brokers, or other external stakeholders is an advantage
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. titleByLocale.en: IAM Integration Engineer - Workforce IAM (Hybrid set up)
titleByLocale.de: IAM Integration Ingenieur - Workforce IAM (Hybrid set up)
titleByLocale.fr: IAM Integration Ingénieur - Workforce IAM (Hybrid set up)

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about identity security and ready to help shape the future of how a global organisation manages
 access? At Swiss Re, we're on a mission to make the world more resilient — and identity is at the heart of that mission. If
 you thrive at the intersection of technology, collaboration, and governance, this is your opportunity to make a real
 impact.
 About the Role

As an IAM Integration Engineer within the Workforce IAM team, you'll play a pivotal role in modernising Swiss Re's identity landscape. You'll be the bridge between application teams and strategic IAM platforms — guiding, assessing, and driving the onboarding of applications to Microsoft Entra ID and SailPoint Identity Security Cloud . This is a hands-on, high-visibility role where your technical expertise, structured thinking, and communication skills will directly contribute to a safer, more scalable identity ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

• Coordinate application integration activities from initial assessment through to completion, working closely with application owners and internal IAM teams.

• Support application onboarding to strategic IAM platforms, including Microsoft Entra ID and SailPoint Identity Security Cloud

• Conduct IAM onboarding and integration assessments — gathering inputs, evaluating integration needs, documenting outcomes, and defining clear next steps

• Analyse existing IAM integrations to identify gaps, risks, inconsistencies, or non-strategic patterns that require remediation

• Guide application teams on onboarding expectations, required actions, and available IAM integration patterns in a clear and accessible way

• Respond to functional and technical IAM queries from application teams, unblocking them through consultation and support, and escalating complex cases to architects or engineers when needed

• Produce clear, structured documentation including meeting summaries, status updates, and follow-up action logs

• Track progress, dependencies, risks, and blockers using tools such as Azure DevOps, Confluence, or internal dashboards

• Coordinate application transitions to strategic IAM solutions by aligning required actions with application owners and internal delivery teams

• Support governance activities by identifying deviations from approved IAM patterns and preparing inputs for exceptions or audit evidence where required
 About the Team

The Security Team at Swiss Re leads all cybersecurity activities across the organisation — spanning engineering, governance, risk, and compliance. Within this team, the Workforce IAM function ensures secure, efficient, and seamless access to digital services for our global workforce.
 We are a collaborative, forward-thinking team currently focused on some of the most exciting challenges in enterprise identity: simplifying identity services, reducing technical debt, improving application onboarding experiences, and driving the transition from legacy IAM patterns to modern, strategic platforms such as Microsoft Entra ID and SailPoint Identity Security Cloud .
 You'll work alongside architects, engineers, compliance specialists, and delivery teams — in an environment that values clear communication, ownership, and continuous improvement. If you're energised by identity integration, cross-team collaboration, and making complex things simple, you'll feel right at home here.
 About You

You're a structured, detail-oriented IAM professional who brings both technical depth and strong interpersonal skills to the table. You know how to navigate complex application landscapes, communicate clearly with diverse stakeholders, and keep multiple workstreams moving forward. You take ownership, follow through, and bring a governance mindset to everything you do.
 You are comfortable working with application teams, clarifying missing information, and turning complex or ambiguous topics into clear actions.

We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• 5+ years of hands-on IAM experience , including application integration, onboarding, migration, or remediation initiatives

• Solid understanding of IAM fundamentals — authentication, authorisation, identity lifecycle, access management, groups, roles, attributes, claims, and provisioning

• Working knowledge of application integration protocols such as SAML, OAuth2, OpenID Connect, and SCIM

• Experience collaborating with application teams or owners to clarify requirements, define actions, and support delivery

• Good understanding of Microsoft Entra ID and enterprise application integration concepts, including Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) principles such as provisioning, access reviews, certifications, RBAC, and application access governance

• Ability to analyse integration scenarios , identify gaps or risks, and translate findings into clear next steps.

• Experience producing IAM documentation, onboarding guidance, or technical enablement materials

• Strong ownership, follow-up discipline, and attention to detail

• Clear and structured communication skills , both written and verbal

• Ability to explain IAM concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Strong English communication skills, both spoken and written
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Experience with SailPoint Identity Security Cloud or similar identity governance platforms

• Experience supporting application onboarding to Microsoft Entra ID or other enterprise IAM platforms

• Familiarity with Active Directory, LDAP, or hybrid identity environments

jobs.title: Data Engineer (Hybrid set up)
jobs.description:
Looking for an opportunity to work on large-scale data challenges, modern data platforms, and solutions that deliver real business impact?
 Join a team that transforms data from around 130 business applications into trusted analytical assets that power more than 200 analytical use cases across Swiss Re's Corporate Solutions (CorSo) business unit. These data assets serve as a single source of truth for a wide range of analytical and reporting needs and are accessed tens of thousands of times each month.
 As a Data Engineer in our D&T CorSo Data Architecture & Engineering team, you'll help create the analytical foundation that enables data-driven decision making across the business.
 Using modern data engineering technologies and AI-assisted development tools, you'll solve complex data challenges, build scalable data products, and transform data into trusted analytical assets used across the business.

About the Role

As a Data Engineer within the D&T CorSo Data Architecture & Engineering team, you'll design, build, and maintain data products that power analytics, reporting, and business decision-making across Swiss Re.
 You'll work mainly with Palantir Foundry and PySpark to build scalable data solutions and transform complex source data into trusted analytical assets. Working closely with stakeholders across the business, you'll help ensure data is accessible, reliable, and fit for a wide range of analytical and reporting needs.
 Beyond data engineering, you'll gain exposure to enterprise-scale data modelling and data governance, providing excellent opportunities to broaden both your technical and architectural expertise.

Key Responsibilities

• Collaborate with customers and stakeholders to deeply understand their data needs and translate the into the integration of data into scalable data solutions that support business processes

• Develop, test, and maintain data pipelines and data management solutions

• Design and implementation of data flows for data ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption

• Contribute to building reliable and scalable data solutions that suport analytics, reporting, and business decision-making

• Improve data transparency through documentation, metadata management, and support for self-service data consumption

• Monitor data pipelines and support data quality, performanc, and reliability while following data engineering standards, best practices, and governance guidelines

About the Team

The D&T CorSo Data Architecture & Engineering team is a collaborative community of more than 50 data engineers and architects working together to enable data-driven decision-making across Swiss Re.
 We value knowledge sharing, engineering excellence, and continuous learning. Whether you're discussing data modelling approaches, optimising distributed processing workloads, or exploring new platform capabilities, you'll have access to experienced colleagues and opportunities to develop both your technical and business domain expertise.

About You

We're looking for someone who brings both technical depth and a genuine curiosity about data. You're someone who takes ownership, communicates clearly, and enjoys working across teams to solve complex data challenges. jobs.description:
About the Role
 You would work closely with Underwriting, supporting with deal acquisition activities/analysis and portfolio overviews, and ensuring that decisions are made based on the most up-to-date and reliable information. You would also be responsible for overall business coordination of an assigned business segment, including ensuring statutory and internal control guidelines are met.
 Key Responsibilities

• Check contract terms and conditions, analyze submission data, investigate, and resolve data issues, review, and report treaty exposure data (Year-over-Year developments, material changes) and load information to costing tools

• Communicate directly with clients, clarify, and follow up on any issues and potentially be part of negotiations

• Enter contractual deal information into systems for consumption by other functions, such as Finance, Accounting, Claims and Reserving

• Lead initiatives with regional / global impact

• Develops role & junior colleagues

• Shares knowledge and drives improvements within XFT
 About the team
 We are a friendly and diverse group of individuals located in Mexico, USA and Brazil with varying levels of experience in the reinsurance industry. We support Latin America Property and Casualty Reinsurance teams and units in delivering on their core mandates. We are part of a global team called Reinsurance Business Operations, and we work closely with our colleagues all over the globe.
 About you
 You’re a strategic and creative thinker when dealing with challenges and opportunities. Your strong interpersonal skills make it easier for you to work within a team. Flexibility and curiosity play a role in your ability to learn new skills quickly.
 Essentials:

• University graduate with a degree in natural science or a quantitative field (Economics, Statistics, Engineering, Actuarial Sciences)

• Minimum 5 years of experience within the Property (Re)insurance industry

• Data savviness and attention to detail, high level of confidence/practical know-how in working with large data files (e.g., NatCat data), MS excel expert skills

• Competent in Microsoft 365 suite, i.e., Power BI, Sharepoint, Powerpoint and Word

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Especially competence in English
 Nice to Haves

• Data modelling and/or previous underwriting experience

• Ambitious and energetic, seeking out new solutions and ways of working

• Adaptable thrive in a work environment where new relationships and projects constantly emerge

• Adeptly prioritize competing tasks and manage timelines

• Strong sense of responsibility, proactive approach, can-do attitude and willingness to go extra mile

• Ability to think independently and suggest appropriate actions to CUW and UWC community
 Our company uses a hybrid work model requiring at least three days in the office each week, with the option to work onsite full-time if preferred. This position is not eligible for full-time telework or visa sponsorship.

jobs.description:
Are you a student in insurance, business administration, or a related field looking to gain real-world experience in a global organization? Join Swiss Re Corporate Solutions in Paris and immerse yourself in the world of corporate insurance through this exciting alternance opportunity. This is your chance to apply what you're learning in the classroom to meaningful, impactful work in a dynamic and international environment — where your contributions matter from day one.
 About the Role
 As an Underwriting Associate Alternant(e), you will play a vital role in supporting our Paris-based underwriting team, ensuring smooth and accurate policy administration while contributing to meaningful process improvement projects. You'll be at the intersection of client service, data management, and operational excellence — developing skills that will set the foundation for a successful career in insurance or business.
 Key 
• Responsibilities
 Policy Administration: Prepare and process invoices, policies, certificates, and all other contractual documentation with precision and care
 Data Management: Compile, sort, review, and verify data accuracy using source documents; detect discrepancies and initiate timely corrections
 System Maintenance: Keep information up to date across internal systems and tools to always ensure data integrity
 Client Interaction: Engage regularly with external stakeholders including brokers and insureds, delivering an outstanding level of service
 Accounting Follow-Up: Support premium chasing, data corrections, and financial monitoring activities
 Process Improvement: Collaborate on the development and maintenance of Standard Operating Procedures, contributing ideas to enhance tools and workflows
 Project Involvement: Participate in cross-functional initiatives that drive operational efficiency and innovation
 About the Team
 You will be joining the Operations EMEA team within Swiss Re Corporate Solutions' Paris office— a vibrant group of 11 experienced professionals from diverse backgrounds, united by a shared commitment to excellence. The team is the backbone of the Paris Corporate Solutions office, acting as the key point of contact for business administration both internally and externally. Known for their collaborative spirit and client-centric approach, the team ensures that brokers, insureds, and internal partners experience a seamless and high-quality service at every touchpoint. You will report directly to the Head of Operations France, based in Paris.

About You
 We're looking for a motivated, curious, and detail-oriented student — ideally pursuing a degree in insurance, business administration, or a related discipline — who thrives in a collaborative, multicultural environment. You bring a positive attitude, a genuine desire to learn, and the ability to manage multiple tasks with care and precision. You're someone who takes initiative, communicates openly, and is committed to delivering quality in everything you do. Whether you're in the early or later stages of your studies, this alternance is designed to give you a strong professional foundation in the insurance industry.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:
 Currently Enrolled in Relevant Studies: Actively pursuing a degree in insurance, business administration, finance, or a related field, with eligibility to undertake an alternance contract
 French & English Proficiency: Strong written and verbal communication skills in both French and English are essential for daily interactions with internal and external stakeholders
 Microsoft Office Skills: Solid working knowledge of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook to support documentation, reporting, and communication tasks
 These are additional nice to have:
 General Insurance Knowledge: A foundational understanding of corporate insurance principles, gained through academic study or prior experience
 Attention to Detail: A quality-focused mindset with the ability to identify errors, flag issues, and propose solutions proactively
 Continuous Learning Mindset: Goal-oriented and enthusiastic about developing new skills in a fast-paced professional environment
 Teamwork & Relationship Building: Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective working relationships across diverse, multicultural teams
 Problem-Solving Ability: Solution-oriented approach with the confidence to identify challenges and escalate appropriately
 Adaptability: Comfort working in a structured yet evolving environment where processes and tools are continuously being refined
 The compensation for this alternance position is determined in accordance with the French legal framework applicable to apprenticeship and professionalization contracts. The salary is calculated based on criteria defined by law, including the apprentice's age, the level of qualification being prepared, and the year of the contract. Details will be discussed transparently during the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Finance Professional
jobs.description:
Join our dynamic team at Swiss Re Group Asset Management and help shape the future of infrastructure finance! We're seeking a talented and motivated professional to contribute to our infrastructure debt investments across diverse sectors and geographies. This role offers an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a growing market while working with a collaborative team of finance experts.

About the Role
 As a valued member of our private infrastructure debt team, you'll play a crucial role in enhancing our lending operations in the North American infrastructure finance market. You'll be involved in the complete investment lifecycle - from origination and due diligence to execution and portfolio management - giving you broad exposure to this exciting asset class.

Key responsibilities include :

• Review and assess private financing deals in the pipeline which are internally originated

• Analyze infrastructure finance transactions including legal, technical and market due diligence, while interrogating financial models and conducting scenario analysis

• Develop and write investment credit memoranda and conduct detailed reviews of transaction documentation

• Establish and maintain a robust investment process and governance framework for internally sourced transactions

• Monitor portfolio performance through quarterly/annual reviews, analysis of the existing portfolio, and reporting on industry trends

• Stay informed about key players and market developments, contributing to investment views and strategies

• Participate actively in regular investment meetings and foster a team-oriented atmosphere of collaboration

About the Team

The Infrastructure Debt team at Swiss Re Group Asset Management is responsible for identifying and executing attractive private infrastructure debt investments across various sectors and geographies. Our team works collaboratively to source, analyze, and manage a growing portfolio of infrastructure assets that provide stable, long-term returns for our clients while contributing to essential infrastructure development worldwide.

About You

We're looking for an open-minded, hard-working, trustworthy and enthusiastic team player who can constructively and respectfully engage in challenging conversations. You thrive when building relationships with clients and external stakeholders and possess strong communication and project management skills with meticulous attention to detail. You're comfortable stepping outside your comfort zone and performing under pressure.

We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements :

• Minimum 2-3 years' experience in banking, asset management or equivalent experience in an infrastructure finance department, preferably in a front-office role

• Strong understanding of technical, legal, commercial and accounting aspects of infrastructure projects, including credit assessment, transaction modelling and execution

• Strong analytical and quantitative skills, including pertinent software know-how

• Written and verbal fluency in English

Additional nice to haves :

• Knowledge of additional languages

• Experience with sustainable or ESG-focused infrastructure investments

• Understanding of insurance company investment requirements

• Experience in different infrastructure sectors (energy, transport, social, digital, etc.)

• International work experience

Our company uses a hybrid work model requiring at least three days in the office each week, with the option to work onsite full-time if preferred. This position is not eligible for full-time telework or visa sponsorship, including OPT.
 The estimated base salary range for this position is $112,000 to $168,000. The specific salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 14,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity
 The North America (US, Canada, English Caribbean) portfolio represents the largest and most complex region within Swiss Re’s L&H reinsurance portfolio.
 The L&H Contracts Team Lead – North America is a senior leadership role with full regional accountability for the Contracts function across traditional reinsurance agreements. This role leads contract drafting discipline, governance rigor, and in-force contractual risk review within a high-volume, performance-driven underwriting environment.
 You will serve as a business partner to Swiss Re L&H's North America Market Units and translate underwriting intent and legal advice into disciplined, repeatable contract execution that protects performance and long-term value. The role owns deviation discipline, negotiation consistency, contractual integrity, and contractual analysis across the region, while driving modernization through workflow tools and GenAI-enabled practices.
 While strong legal and drafting expertise is essential, this role sits within the L&H Pricing & Portfolio Performance (PPP) function and partners closely with legal, underwriting, pricing, claims, portfolio management and risk functions to support Swiss Re's North America business. It is accountable for ensuring contracts reflect disciplined risk-taking and align with underwriting performance objectives.
 Reporting to the Global Head of L&H Contracts, this role is a member of the global L&H Contracts Leadership Team and plays a visible role in shaping the evolution of the Contracts function.
 About the Life & Health Contracts Function
 The L&H Contracts function at Swiss Re drafts, reviews and advises on reinsurance agreements between Swiss Re and its clients. In close partnership with underwriting, pricing, claims, legal, and risk, the team:

• Structures and documents traditional reinsurance agreements

• Ensures contractual terms reflect underwriting intent

• Provides clear advice on wording implications and risk trade-offs

• Supports disciplined portfolio management through contracts analysis
 Contracts plays a critical role in safeguarding Swiss Re’s risk position while enabling sustainable long-term profitability.
 Your Mandate
 1. Strengthen Commercial Discipline

• Ensure contracts reflect underwriting intent and disciplined risk-taking

• Act as a trusted partner to Client Markets and cross-functional stakeholders (Underwriting, Pricing, Claims, Legal), shaping deal structure and contract outcomes on key accounts

• Provide clear, decisive recommendations on wording and structural trade-offs, including hands-on involvement of key client accounts

• Lead interpretation, analysis, and restructuring of existing agreements
 2. Strengthen Governance & Standardization

• Ensure consistent application of global contracting standards

• Own deviation governance, tracking, and transparency across the region

• Strengthen documentation rigor and decision traceability
 3. Talent Management & Leadership

• Lead, mentor, and develop team of Contracts Specialists across the US and Canada

• Define clear roles, accountability, and career pathways for Contracts Specialists

• Represent North America within the global L&H Contracts Leadership Team
 4. Accelerate Digital Workflow & GenAI Adoption

• Lead regional adoption of contracting workflow tools and GenAI-enabled practices, embedding AI into standard drafting and review workflows

• Ensure responsible use of GenAI is operationally embedded and scalable across the region
 What Success Looks Like
 Within 18–24 months:

• Contracts is recognized as a disciplined commercial and risk partner across North America

• Strong governance and deviation discipline across markets

• Broad adoption of digital workflow and GenAI tools
 Your Profile

• 12–15+ years’ experience in Life & Health reinsurance or insurance contracting - must have Law degree

• Strong legal foundation or substantial experience drafting and negotiating reinsurance agreements

• Demonstrated commercial judgment and ability to articulate risk trade-offs

• Experience operating in a regulated, high-complexity reinsurance environment

• Experience leading multi-location teams

• Experience driving workflow modernization and technology-enabled change
 You are:

• A high-accountability leader who drives performance and sets clear standards

• Decisive and comfortable owning difficult calls

• Commercially pragmatic while uncompromising on risk discipline

• Confident challenging stakeholders constructively

• Committed to developing talent and strengthening capabilities
 Why This Role Is Compelling

• Full regional accountability across Swiss Re’s largest L&H portfolio

• Direct partnership with the North America leadership and the Global Head of L&H Contracts

• Mandate to strengthen commercial discipline and governance at scale

• Opportunity to shape the evolution of the Contracts function, including integration of workflow and GenAI
 The base salary hiring range for this existing position is CAD $170,000 - 204,000. The specific base salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.
 Our company has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office three days per week.
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 14,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

These tools provide additional insights to our recruitment teams, but all hiring decisions are carefully reviewed and made by people. jobs.description:
Bereit, Ihre Risiko- und Finanzexpertise in einem dynamischen, globalen Umfeld einzusetzen? Werden Sie Teil von Swiss Re Corporate Solutions und unterstützen unsere europäischen Kunden bei ihrem weltweiten Bürgschafts- und Garantiebedarf.
 Über die Position
 Als Underwriter Surety mit Sitz in Frankfurt verbinden Sie analytische Kenntnisse mit Kundenmanagement und arbeiten mit Unternehmen und Maklern in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz zusammen. Die Rolle bietet die perfekte Balance zwischen Risiko-Underwriting und kundenbezogenen Aufgaben in einem unternehmerischen Umfeld.
 Hauptaufgaben

• Durchführung von Risikoprüfungen für neue und bestehende Kunden, im Einklang mit bestehendem Risikoappetit und höchster Kundenzufriedenheit

• Verantwortung für eigenes Kundenportfolio und Transaktionen sowie die Erschließung neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten in Europa, insbesondere in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz

• Analyse und Bewertung von Kredit- und Transaktionsrisiken in enger Abstimmung mit internen Stakeholdern

• Genehmigung von Transaktionen innerhalb eigener Kompetenzen sowie Erstellung strukturierter Gremienvorlagen

• Aufbau und Betreuung von Kunden und Maklerbeziehungen durch regelmäßige persönliche Gespräche

• Monitoring des eigenen Kundenportfolios unter Einbeziehung interner und externer Informationen

• Marktanalysen in Bezug auf Veränderungen im Underwriting-, Markt- und rechtlichen Umfeld, sowie deren Risikoauswirkungen
 Über das Team
 Als Teil der Swiss Re Group mit einer 150-jährigen Geschichte ist Swiss Re Corporate Solutions ein wichtiger Partner bei der Lösung von Risikomanagement- und Finanzierungsbedürfnissen von Unternehmen weltweit. Mit Fokus auf eine ergebnisorientierte Underwriting-Kultur suchen wir eine teamorientierte Persönlichkeit, zur Verstärkung unseres wachsenden Teams eines der führenden Anbieter von Bürgschafts- und Garantielösungen.
 Über Sie
 Sie bringen Ihre analytischen Fähigkeiten und Engagement gerne in einem internationalen teamorientierten Umfeld ein und arbeiten gerne mit Kunden und Vertriebspartnern zusammen.
 Wir suchen Kandidaten, die folgende Anforderungen erfüllen:

• Mindestens 3 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung, vorzugsweise in einer Bank oder bei einem Kautionsversicherer

• Selbstbewusste Persönlichkeit mit starken Kommunikationsfähigkeiten für den Umgang mit Kunden, Geschäftspartnern und Kollegen

• Fähigkeit effizient in einem teamorientierten Umfeld zu arbeiten

• Analytische Entscheidungsfähigkeit und Lösungsorientierung

• Verständnis von Kreditrisiken und Finanzmärkten, insbesondere in Bezug auf Fremdfinanzierung

• Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und fließende Englischkenntnisse
 In Deutschland liegt das Grundgehalt für diese Position zwischen 71.000 EUR und 118.000 EUR (Vollzeitbeschäftigung). Das konkrete Gehaltsangebot berücksichtigt:

• Anforderungen, Umfang, Komplexität und Verantwortung der Position

• Das Profil des Bewerbers/der Bewerberin, einschließlich Ausbildung/Qualifikationen, Fachwissen, Spezialisierung, Fähigkeiten und Erfahrung
 Zusätzlich zu Ihrem Grundgehalt bietet Swiss Re eine attraktive, leistungsbezogene variable Vergütungskomponente, die Ihre Leistungen anerkennt. Darüber hinaus profitieren Sie von einer Vielzahl globaler und standortspezifischer Leistungen.
 Die Anspruchsberechtigung kann je nach den Bedingungen der Swiss Re und Ihrem Arbeitsvertrag variieren.
 About Swiss Re Corporate Solutions
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer. We anticipate and manage risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime.

Swiss Re Corporate Solutions is the commercial insurance arm of the Swiss Re Group. We offer innovative insurance solutions to large and midsized multinational corporations from our approximately 50 locations worldwide. We help clients mitigate their risk exposure, whilst our industry-leading claims service provides them with additional peace of mind.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. Swiss Re Corporate Solutions embraces a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

jobs.description:
Locations:
Alpharetta, GA, US |
Kansas City, MO, US |
New York, NY, US |
Windsor, CT, US |
Los Angeles, CA, US |
Chicago, IL, US |
Armonk, NY, US

Swiss Re is building a next-generation platform for corporates combining proprietary risk data, advanced analytics, and deep risk expertise to deliver actionable insights at scale. We are now looking for a high-performing sales hunter to lead new business acquisition across the United States.
 About the Role
 This is a rare opportunity to take an emerging, high-value proposition to market and win strategic, first-of-their-kind deals with large corporates! You will operate in a greenfield environment, shaping the go-to-market, opening new logos, and helping scale a business at the intersection of risk, data, and technology.
 Key responsibilities include :

• Own new logo acquisition across the United States, targeting large corporates and risk leaders (CROs, CFOs, Heads of Risk)

• Build and execute a territory and account penetration strategy to exceed revenue targets

• Originate, develop, and close complex enterprise deals

• Establish and manage senior C-level relationships

• Lead cross-functional deal teams across product, underwriting, engineering, and partners

• Shape compelling commercial propositions and business cases

• Bring market feedback into product development

• Define and scale repeatable go-to-market approaches
 What Makes This Role Different?

• Greenfield builder role – not account management

• Opportunity to land flagship clients

• Backed by Swiss Re’s brand and data capabilities

• Exposure to climate, supply chain, and property risk topics
 About You
 You have a proven track record of winning new logos and successfully closing early-stage or category-creating deals. You possess strong C-level engagement skills and solid ability to effectively lead complex deal teams. Thriving in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, you bring a strategic mindset to drive growth!
 Additional Requirements Include :

• 5–10+ years in enterprise new business sales

• Experience selling enterprise SaaS, data, AI, or cloud platforms

• Consistent quota overachievement

• US enterprise sales experience preferred

• Fluent business English
 Nice to Have :

• Understanding of commercial risk or insurance markets

• Exposure to climate, supply chain, or property risks

• Experience selling to risk management, finance, or operations executives
 Working Model

• US-based, covering a designated territory

• Travel up to 30%
 About the Team
 The Risk Data Solutions (RDS) team is on a mission to revolutionize how corporates understand and manage risk with bold, innovative solutions designed to deliver outstanding risk insights and expertise to corporate customers We are a team of builders, thinkers, and doers who are passionate about creating something genuinely new in the risk intelligence space. Joining RDS means being part of something from the ground up, backed by the credibility and capabilities of Swiss Re.
 The estimated base salary range for this position in Kansas City, Chicago, Windsor, CT and Alpharetta $140,000 to $210,000 and for Armonk, New York and Los Angeles is $152,000 to $228,000. The specific salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.

Swiss Re is an equal opportunity employer. It is our practice to recruit, hire and promote without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, pregnancy, sexual orientations, marital status, military status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Decisions on employment are solely based on an individual's qualifications for the position being filled.

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about navigating the complex world of global sanctions compliance? Join our dynamic team at Swiss Re where you'll play a pivotal role in designing and implementing strategies that control our exposure to the sanctions risk while enabling compliant business operations worldwide.
 We are open to considering candidates based in other locations.
 About the Role
 As our Sanctions Risk Framework Owner, you'll be the driving force behind Swiss Re's global sanctions compliance strategy. You'll design, oversee, and continuously evolve our global sanctions risk framework, bringing together your expertise in sanctions regimes, interpretation of sanctions developments, and their application to the insurance industry with a strategic mindset.
 Key Responsibilities

• Own and enhance the global Sanctions Risk Framework , including policies, standards, and processes that form the foundation of our sanctions risk management approach.

• Monitor and interpret sanctions developments from relevant authorities, translating them into impact on our business.

• Develop and coordinate responses , including approvals, communication and implementation across the company.

• Provide ongoing oversight of the design and effectiveness of the sanctions control environment.

• Provide expert advisory support to senior stakeholders on sanctions topics and develop position papers to enable consistent guidance across business units.

• Own and drive the implementation and ongoing effectiveness of sanction controls in screening and related tools.

• Lead training and awareness by developing comprehensive training material for employees, conducting trainings, and supporting the growth of sanctions expertise within Compliance teams.

• Drive continuous improvement of our compliance processes and controls, contributing to the broader financial crime risk management strategy.
 Please note that this role does not involve hands-on screening, alert handling, or KYC case processing.
 About the Team
 The Compliance Financial Crime Risk Frameworks (FCR) team is responsible for global Compliance frameworks covering four key financial crime risks: Fraud, Bribery and Corruption, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, and Economic Sanctions. We develop, maintain, and implement global policies, standards, processes, and supporting technology to manage these risks effectively. Our diverse team spans New York, Bratislava, and London, working collaboratively to monitor emerging risks and regulatory developments across all jurisdictions where Swiss Re operates.
 About You
 You're a detail-oriented compliance professional with deep sanctions expertise across sanctions regimes and excellent communication skills. You thrive in a collaborative environment while being capable of working independently on complex sanctions matters. Your analytical mindset enables you to translate regulatory requirements into practical frameworks and solutions.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

•
• Strong Compliance experience , including at least 5 years focused on Sanctions topics, ideally within the insurance industry.

• Deep expertise in financial, economic and trade sanctions .

• Proven experience in translating sanctions developments across regimes, regulations and programs into business impact and risk responses.

• Sound experience in risk frameworks , particularly in drafting policies, standards, and processes, and maintaining a Compliance Risk framework.

• University or equivalent qualification with fluency in English (written and spoken); legal training would be beneficial.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to engage effectively with colleagues across all seniority levels.

These would be a plus:

• Certified Global Sanctions Specialist (CGSS) or another professional sanctions certification

• Knowledge of other financial crime risks (Fraud, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, and Bribery and Corruption)

• Additional languages, especially German

• Experience developing and delivering compliance training programs

• Strong project and change management skills
 Compensation & Work Model
 For Slovakia, the monthly base salary range for this position is between 2,900 EUR and 4,900 EUR for a full-time role.
 The specific salary offered considers:
 • the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role
 • the applicant's own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialisation, skills and experience
 In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for additional rewards and benefits including an attractive performance-based bonus.
 We provide feedback to all candidates via email. If you have not heard back from us, please check your spam folder.
 #LI-Hybri
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 14,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.
 We may use AI-powered tools to support the review and evaluation of applications for this position. These tools provide additional insights to our recruitment teams, but all hiring decisions are carefully reviewed and made by people. To learn more about how we use AI in recruitment and how we handle your personal data, please review our Data Privacy Statement before applying.
