jobs.description:
About the Role
 In this pivotal role, you'll bridge the gap between business needs and technical implementation, ensuring our insurance products deliver exceptional value. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate complex requirements into clear specifications that guide our development process.
 Key Responsibilities

• Analyze and clarify business requirements and translate them into functional and technical specifications including business architecture, process maps, wireframes and data models

• Ensure comprehensive specification of User Stories with all required data and background analysis available to the entire team

• Design and define related test cases and support the Product Owner in creating effective acceptance criteria

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Platform Product Owners, Technology Leads, Business Process Managers, Business Architecture and the Data Office to maintain end-to-end consistency of system, process and information architecture

• Anticipate and analyze customer needs to develop effective problem-solving solutions

• Organize and prioritize the Product Backlog based on Product Owner guidance

• Own production support for one or more business applications, addressing user requests directly or triaging more complex cases to the development team

• Create and maintain comprehensive project documentation on the corporate Wiki

About the Team
 Our team is responsible for building products and solutions for the Corporate Solutions business unit. We work in a collaborative, innovative environment where your ideas will have real impact. We partner closely with colleagues around the globe, fostering a diverse and inclusive atmosphere where different perspectives help shape exceptional insurance products. As part of our team, you'll contribute to meaningful projects while developing your skills in a supportive, growth-oriented culture.
 What You Bring

• Experience as a Product Owner or in a similar role

• Practical knowledge of agile delivery

• Ability to work effectively with both business and technical teams

• Clear communication and stakeholder‑management skills

• General technical understanding of software or data‑enabled products
 Relevant university degree or equivalent professional experience
 About You
 You're a detail-oriented problem solver who thrives in collaborative environments. You have excellent analytical skills and can effectively translate between business and technical domains. You're proactive, customer-focused, and committed to delivering high-quality solutions that drive business value.
 We need you to bring in the following must haves:

• 5+ years of experience as a Requirements Engineer or in similar roles

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills

• Strong grasp of Agile methodologies and experience working in cross-functional product teams

• Proficiency in tools like Jira or similar Agile management platforms like Azure DevOps

• Proficient in Visio, Figma or other process mapping tools, with good knowledge of BPMN

These are additional nice to haves:

• Experience with Commercial Insurance products and processes

• Knowledge of insurance industry standards and regulations

• Experience with data modeling and database concepts

• Background in software development or technical implementation

jobs.title: Modelling Lead Americas
jobs.description:
Locations:
Fort Wayne, IN, US |
Armonk, NY, US

Are you a seasoned leader with deep expertise in Life & Health valuation and a passion for building future-ready modelling solutions? If you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and love uniting diverse teams around a shared purpose, this could be the role for you!

About the Role
 As the Modelling Lead Americas, you will be at the heart of Swiss Re's actuarial and financial modelling capabilities, driving the development, maintenance, and execution of critical valuation models. Your remit spans a broad and exciting geographic scope — covering Life & Health products across the US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability products in Australia — making this a truly global leadership opportunity. You will play a pivotal role in shaping the strategic direction of modelling across these regions, ensuring our models are robust, forward-looking, and aligned with evolving regulatory and reporting standards. This is a rare opportunity to make a lasting impact at the intersection of technical excellence and strategic leadership.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead and inspire a diverse, high-performing modelling team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement

• Develop, maintain, and run Life & Health valuation models across US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability models for Australia , ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with business objectives

• Drive financial reporting excellence across US Statutory, IFRS and local statutory reporting frameworks, ensuring compliance and consistency across all regions

• Design and implement future-ready modelling solutions , anticipating business needs and regulatory changes across multiple jurisdictions

• Manage strategic relationships with external modelling and technology vendors , ensuring solutions meet business needs, deliver value, and support the long-term evolution of the modelling ecosystem

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Swiss Re's actuarial, finance, and technology teams to deliver integrated, end-to-end modelling capabilities

• Manage model governance, validation, and documentation standards, ensuring models are robust, accurate, fit for purpose, and supported by transparent, auditable processes.

• Navigate ambiguity and complexity with confidence, providing clear direction and pragmatic solutions in a rapidly evolving, multi-regional landscape

• Engage senior stakeholders , communicating complex modelling concepts and results in a clear, compelling, and accessible manner

• Mentor and develop team members , building technical depth and leadership capability across the modelling function

About the Team
 The Modelling Centre of Excellence (MCoE) Americas is a dynamic and collaborative team dedicated to developing, maintaining, and running critical valuation models representing more than half of Swiss Re's Life & Health exposure globally. The team's scope spans Life & Health products across the US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability products in Australia , reflecting the breadth and diversity of Swiss Re's reinsurance portfolio. The team plays a critical role in supporting Swiss Re's financial reporting and strategic decision-making, combining deep technical expertise with a forward-thinking approach to modelling innovation.

About You
 You are a seasoned valuation and modelling professional and an inspiring leader who brings both deep technical expertise and a strategic mindset to everything you do. You are resilient, calm under pressure, and skilled at navigating complexity and ambiguity across diverse geographies and product lines. You have a natural ability to unite diverse teams around shared goals, and you are passionate about designing solutions that are not just fit for today, but ready for tomorrow.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• Expert knowledge of Life & Health products , including valuation methodologies and financial reporting frameworks across US, Canada, Latin America, and Australia

• Deep expertise in L&H Valuation and Financial Reporting , with hands-on experience in both US Statutory and IFRS standards

• Strong technical understanding of actuarial and finance systems , including proficiency with Moody's AXIS modelling platform

• Strong leadership experience, with the ability to develop high-performing, geographically diverse teams and unite cross-functional stakeholders around shared objectives.
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Resilience and composure under pressure , with the ability to deliver high-quality outcomes in fast-moving, high-stakes environments

• Skilled in managing ambiguity and resolving conflicts , bringing clarity and direction when challenges arise

• Strategic mindset , with demonstrated ability to design and implement future-ready, scalable solutions

• Experience working in a global or matrixed organization , navigating complex stakeholder landscapes across geographies

The position will be located in our Fort Wayne, IN or Armonk, NY office. Our company uses a hybrid work model requiring at least three days in the office each week, with the option to work onsite full-time if preferred. This position is not eligible for full-time telework or relocation assistance.

For Fort Wayne, the estimated base salary range for this position is $146,000 to $244,000. For Armonk, the estimated base salary range for this position is $154,000 to $256,000. The specific salary offered for this, or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.

About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.

Swiss Re is an equal opportunity employer. It is our practice to recruit, hire and promote without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, pregnancy, sexual orientations, marital status, military status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Decisions on employment are solely based on an individual's qualifications for the position being filled.

During the recruitment process, reasonable accommodations for disabilities are available upon request. If contacted for an interview, please inform the Recruiter/HR Professional of the accommodation needed.

jobs.description:
Engineering Underwriter, Swiss Re India Branch
 Are you a detail-oriented insurance professional with a passion for engineering risk and a drive to make a real impact in one of the world's most dynamic markets? This is your opportunity to join a global reinsurance leader and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of engineering underwriting in India.

About the Role
 As an Engineering Underwriter, you will be at the heart of our underwriting operations — bridging analytical excellence with client-focused solutions. You will partner closely with senior underwriters to drive economic profit growth, delivering sharp pre-underwriting analysis and seamless post-underwriting support across treaty and facultative engineering business. This role offers a unique blend of technical depth and market exposure.
 Key Responsibilities

• Drive economic profit growth by providing high-quality analytical support to senior underwriters in India, enabling informed underwriting decisions on engineering treaty and facultative business

• Conduct thorough exposure assessments, input pricing data into systems, and prepare pre-underwriting notes for review by Engineering Underwriters

• Complete post-underwriting activities accurately and efficiently in the system upon finalization of business by the underwriter

• Analyse client requests from the Indian market and deliver well-reasoned recommendations on engineering treaty and facultative business

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support deal-team solutions and client needs

• Contribute to and exchange knowledge within the Engineering Underwriting community, sharing insights and best practices across the global network

• Stay informed on global Engineering market trends and developments, applying specialist know-how to add value to clients and client teams in India

• Bring a collaborative mindset and technical expertise to cross-functional initiatives

About the Team
 Our Engineering Underwriting team in India is a dynamic and collaborative group dedicated to growing and managing a high-quality engineering reinsurance portfolio across treaty and facultative lines. The team works closely with global underwriting communities to deliver tailored, innovative solutions to clients across the Indian market. With a strong focus on knowledge sharing, technical excellence, and market development, the team plays a strategic role in Swiss Re's presence and growth in one of the world's most exciting insurance markets.

About You
 You are a curious and analytically minded professional who thrives in a collaborative environment and is eager to deepen your expertise in engineering reinsurance. You bring a structured approach to problem-solving, communicate complex ideas with clarity, and are motivated by contributing to a high-performing team. You are entrepreneurial, proactive, and detail-oriented — someone who takes ownership and is passionate about building deep knowledge in a specialised and globally relevant field.
 The successful candidate will demonstrate the following core professional attributes, which are considered essential to performing effectively in this role and integral to our team culture:

• Collaborative team orientation — ability to work cohesively within a team, actively contributing to shared goals and supporting colleagues across all levels

• Adaptability — the capacity to respond constructively to changing priorities, evolving business needs, and new challenges with composure and professionalism

• Open-mindedness — a genuine willingness to consider diverse perspectives, embrace new ideas, and engage with different approaches to problem-solving

• Interpersonal effectiveness — the ability to build positive, productive working relationships with colleagues, clients, and stakeholders in a professional and approachable manner
 We are looking for candidates with the following requirements:

• 3–8 years of insurance industry experience or reinsurance sector, with underwriting experience preferred

• On-ground experience in the construction industry, providing practical understanding of engineering risks and project environments is preferred

• Engineering qualification — a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Civil, Mechanical Engineering from a recognised government or elite private institution

• A Master's in Business Administration from the National Insurance Academy or an equivalent (re)insurance-specialised institution is an added advantage
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Familiarity with the Indian insurance or reinsurance market and its regulatory landscape

• Experience working with pricing tools or underwriting systems and inputting/managing technical data

• Exposure to claims advisory or coverage analysis in an engineering context

• Entrepreneurial mindset — a sense of urgency, cost-consciousness, and willingness to take calculated risks, with a commitment to sustainable performance and continuous improvement

• Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage peak-period workloads effectively

• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment, adapting seamlessly to a fast-paced and evolving landscape

• Creative thinking and problem-solving attitude, with a proactive approach to challenges

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

jobs.title: Technical Sales Lead - PSS
jobs.description:
About the Role
 We are seeking a highly motivated professional with a growth-oriented mindset and a collaborative approach. We welcome candidates with 5–10 years of experience in structuring and selling risk transfer solutions, ideally with a focus on natural catastrophe and climate risks.
 As part of the global Technical Sales team, you will work closely with regional Public Sector Solutions (PSS) client management teams, as well as underwriting and structuring experts across Swiss Re’s business units. In this role, you will represent PSS solution capabilities within your region and help deliver client-ready, value-adding solutions tailored to evolving client needs.
 You will combine your expertise with Swiss Re’s extensive technical capabilities, collaborating across functions to design and implement innovative risk transfer solutions. We value strong analytical, structuring, and underwriting skills, and we also support continuous learning and development in these areas.
 Equally important is your ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and accessibly, both in writing and verbally, to a wide range of audiences, including non-experts, to support impactful client engagement.
 The role involves frequent interaction with public sector clients, brokers, modelling firms, and data providers across various levels of seniority.
 Key accountabilities include :

• Represent Swiss Re’s technical expertise in natural catastrophe and climate risks, with a particular focus on the Americas. Introduce, explain, and help prepare underwriting-ready solutions.

• Promote and leverage the full spectrum of Swiss Re’s products and solutions across multiple lines of business, supporting sustainable and scalable business growth.

• Contribute to sales effectiveness by strengthening client relationships, communicating clearly, and applying thoughtful sales approaches to improve conversion rates.

• Support large-scale PSS transactions and development projects, spanning structuring, underwriting, and product and solution development.

• Collaborate closely with product experts and local client-facing teams, including in client interactions, to ensure high-quality and effective delivery of solutions and to represent technical expertise within the region.

• Act as a bridge between client needs and Swiss Re’s capabilities by translating complex technical content into clear, accessible language and compelling illustrations.

• Improve efficiency by helping replicate successful transactions, enhancing overall effectiveness and the economics of PSS transaction management.

• Key performance measures include but are not limited to:
(i) managing a deal pipeline,
(ii) improving business conversion rates, and
(iii) growing bound business volume.
 About the Team
 Governments and public sector entities are increasingly aware of the risks they bear as both explicit and implicit risk holders. Over the past 16 years, Swiss Re has invested significantly in partnerships with public sector stakeholders to deepen understanding of this evolving risk landscape and to demonstrate how risk transfer solutions can help address emerging fiscal and societal challenges.
 The continued success of Public Sector Solutions (PSS) represents a strong opportunity for further growth, reinforcing the public sector as a key pillar of Swiss Re’s broader strategy across its (re)insurance and capital markets businesses. By supporting our clients, we contribute to economic development, strengthen risk awareness, and enhance societal resilience.
 Our ambition is to systematically grow public sector business by engaging national and municipal governments, NGOs, and development banks through a coordinated, Group-wide approach. We provide tailored risk transfer solutions that help reduce governments’ contingent liabilities—ranging from innovative structures such as pandemic catastrophe bonds to reinsurance solutions supporting small and medium-sized enterprises in the context of a changing climate.
 While our solutions span a wide range of risks, natural catastrophes and climate-related exposures remain central to both our business and our impact.
 To support our growth ambitions, we are seeking a Technical Sales Lead for the with focus on Canada but global reach and impact. This role is suited to someone motivated by complex challenges and eager to contribute to Public Sector Solutions in a technically focused, client-facing environment.
 About You

• 5–10 years of relevant professional experience, for example in underwriting, risk assessment, risk modelling, or applied sciences (e.g. earthquake, tropical cyclone, flood, or climate risk). Experience with index-based (parametric) risk transfer solutions is an advantage.

• Strong interest in origination and sales, with an initial track record of building relevant industry networks. Confident communicator, able to bridge the “science” of risk assessment with the “application” of risk transfer solutions.

• Experience in the insurance industry, insurtech, broker organisations, or related fields. A broad and active industry network is a plus.

• Academic background in a STEM-related discipline (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics), ideally with a master’s degree or higher, and strong familiarity with quantitative environments.

• Proven ability to translate complex technical topics into clear, accessible content for client-facing discussions and commercial decision-making.

• Proactive and collaborative working style, with the ability to operate effectively in a global environment, including across virtual and cross-time-zone teams.

• Strong team player, comfortable taking on different roles in a dynamic and evolving environment and motivated to collaborate across functions and geographies.

• Persistence and resilience, with the ability to balance strategic thinking and attention to detail.

• Ability to support transaction execution responsibly and efficiently, in line with internal processes and with a focus on sustainable profitability.
 The base salary hiring range for this new position located in Toronto is CAD $150,000 to $200,000. The specific base salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.
 About Swiss Re Corporate Solutions
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer. We anticipate and manage risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime.

Swiss Re Corporate Solutions is the commercial insurance arm of the Swiss Re Group. We offer innovative insurance solutions to large and midsized multinational corporations from our approximately 50 locations worldwide. We help clients mitigate their risk exposure, whilst our industry-leading claims service provides them with additional peace of mind.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. Swiss Re Corporate Solutions embraces a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.

Swiss Re is an equal opportunity employer. It is our practice to recruit, hire and promote without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, pregnancy, sexual orientations, marital status, military status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Decisions on employment are solely based on an individual's qualifications for the position being filled.

During the recruitment process, reasonable accommodations for disabilities are available upon request. If contacted for an interview, please inform the Recruiter/HR Professional of the accommodation needed.

These tools provide additional insights to our recruitment teams, but all hiring decisions are carefully reviewed and made by people.  As part of the global Technical Sales team, you will work closely with regional Public Sector Solutions (PSS) client management teams, as well as underwriting and structuring experts across Swiss Re’s business units. In this role, you will represent PSS solution capabilities within your region and help deliver client-ready, value-adding solutions tailored to evolving client needs.
 You will combine your expertise with Swiss Re’s extensive technical capabilities, collaborating across functions to design and implement innovative risk transfer solutions. We value strong analytical, structuring, and underwriting skills, and we also support continuous learning and development in these areas.
 Equally important is your ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and accessibly, both in writing and verbally, to a wide range of audiences, including non-experts, to support impactful client engagement.
 The role involves frequent interaction with public sector clients, brokers, modelling firms, and data providers across various levels of seniority.
 Key accountabilities include :

• Represent Swiss Re’s technical expertise in natural catastrophe and climate risks, with a particular focus on the Americas. Introduce, explain, and help prepare underwriting-ready solutions.

• Promote and leverage the full spectrum of Swiss Re’s products and solutions across multiple lines of business, supporting sustainable and scalable business growth.

• Contribute to sales effectiveness by strengthening client relationships, communicating clearly, and applying thoughtful sales approaches to improve conversion rates.

• Support large-scale PSS transactions and development projects, spanning structuring, underwriting, and product and solution development.

• Collaborate closely with product experts and local client-facing teams, including in client interactions, to ensure high-quality and effective delivery of solutions and to represent technical expertise within the region.

• Act as a bridge between client needs and Swiss Re’s capabilities by translating complex technical content into clear, accessible language and compelling illustrations.

• Improve efficiency by helping replicate successful transactions, enhancing overall effectiveness and the economics of PSS transaction management.

• Key performance measures include but are not limited to:
(i) managing a deal pipeline,
(ii) improving business conversion rates, and
(iii) growing bound business volume.
 About the Team
 Governments and public sector entities are increasingly aware of the risks they bear as both explicit and implicit risk holders. Over the past 16 years, Swiss Re has invested significantly in partnerships with public sector stakeholders to deepen understanding of this evolving risk landscape and to demonstrate how risk transfer solutions can help address emerging fiscal and societal challenges.
 The continued success of Public Sector Solutions (PSS) represents a strong opportunity for further growth, reinforcing the public sector as a key pillar of Swiss Re’s broader strategy across its (re)insurance and capital markets businesses. By supporting our clients, we contribute to economic development, strengthen risk awareness, and enhance societal resilience.
 Our ambition is to systematically grow public sector business by engaging national and municipal governments, NGOs, and development banks through a coordinated, Group-wide approach. We provide tailored risk transfer solutions that help reduce governments’ contingent liabilities—ranging from innovative structures such as pandemic catastrophe bonds to reinsurance solutions supporting small and medium-sized enterprises in the context of a changing climate.
 While our solutions span a wide range of risks, natural catastrophes and climate-related exposures remain central to both our business and our impact.

• 5–10 years of relevant professional experience, for example in underwriting, risk assessment, risk modelling, or applied sciences (e.g. earthquake, tropical cyclone, flood, or climate risk). Experience with index-based (parametric) risk transfer solutions is an advantage.

• Experience in the insurance industry, insurtech, broker organisations, or related fields. A broad and active industry network is a plus.

• Academic background in a STEM-related discipline (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics), ideally with a master’s degree or higher, and strong familiarity with quantitative environments.

• Proven ability to translate complex technical topics into clear, accessible content for client-facing discussions and commercial decision-making.

• Proactive and collaborative working style, with the ability to operate effectively in a global environment, including across virtual and cross-time-zone teams.

• Strong team player, comfortable taking on different roles in a dynamic and evolving environment and motivated to collaborate across functions and geographies.

• Persistence and resilience, with the ability to balance strategic thinking and attention to detail.

• Ability to support transaction execution responsibly and efficiently, in line with internal processes and with a focus on sustainable profitability.

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about shaping the future of risk governance? Do you thrive at the intersection of policy design, stakeholder collaboration, and operational risk oversight? If so, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact at one of the world's leading reinsurance companies.
 About the Role
 As an Operational Risk Policy Governance Analyst at Swiss Re, you will play a pivotal role in building and shaping a central second line of defence (2LoD) policy governance capability for selected operational risks, including emerging and evolving areas such as AI, Data Management, and Records Management. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to the design of clear, consistent, and effective policy frameworks that drive sustainable governance across the organisation. You will work closely with first-line teams and subject matter experts, bringing structure, rigour, and insight to the full policy lifecycle—from architecture and guardrails through to approvals, periodic review, and continuous improvement.
 Key Responsibilities:

• Develop and maintain policy architecture — design and evolve the structural framework for selected operational risk policies, ensuring clarity, consistency, and alignment with Swiss Re's governance standards

• Define policy requirements and guardrails — draft clear, concise, and practical policy requirements that provide effective second line oversight and guidance to first line teams

• Coordinate approvals and periodic reviews — manage governance processes end-to-end, ensuring timely approvals, structured review cycles, and accurate documentation

• Support end-to-end policy lifecycle management and reporting — oversee the full lifecycle of policies from inception through to retirement, maintaining high-quality records and producing meaningful governance reporting

• Provide trusted second line oversight and constructive challenge — act as a credible and collaborative partner to first line teams and subject matter experts, offering sound judgement and independent perspective on governance matters

• Engage and manage stakeholders across functions and seniority levels — build and maintain strong professional networks, communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences

• Contribute to continuous improvement — proactively identify opportunities to enhance policy governance processes, frameworks, and tools in a dynamic and evolving risk environment
 About the Team
 The ORM Policy Governance team sits within Group Functions Risk Management (GFRM) at Swiss Re. The team is responsible for building and maintaining a central 2LoD policy governance capability for selected operational risks, working across the organisation to ensure that policy requirements are clear, robust, and fit for purpose. The team collaborates closely with first line teams and subject matter experts to promote consistent, sustainable governance across a broad range of evolving operational risk topics — from AI and Data Management to Records Management and beyond.
 About You
 You are a detail-oriented, collaborative, and proactive professional with a genuine interest inoperational risk governance and policy design. You bring strong analytical and communicationskills, a structured working style, and the confidence to engage and challenge constructivelyacross all levels of the organisation. You are comfortable navigating complexity, managingmultiple priorities, and contributing meaningfully to a team that values knowledge sharing,curiosity, and continuous improvement.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• 5+ years of experience in Operational risk management expertise — relevant experience in operational risk management, financial or non-financial risk governance, or a comparable control/governance environment within insurance or financial services

• Policy governance experience — demonstrated experience in policy drafting, policy review, governance processes, or lifecycle management, with a strong ability to write clear, concise, and practical policy requirements

• Understanding of the three lines of defence model — solid grasp of operational risk management concepts and governance frameworks, with the ability to apply sound judgement on governance matters

• Academic foundation — university degree in business, finance, law, risk management, or a related field (or equivalent studies)

• Communication and stakeholder engagement skills — strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to engage effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders and challenge constructively
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Experience working in a second line of defence or oversight function within a large, complex organisation

• Familiarity with evolving operational risk topics such as AI governance, data management, or records management

• Experience working in a multinational or cross-cultural environment

• Proficiency in MS Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

• Strong organisational skills with high attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple topics and deadlines simultaneously

• A collaborative mindset with a passion for knowledge sharing and continuous improvement

• Ability to switch fluidly between detailed analytical work and strategic, big-picture thinking
 For Slovakia the base salary range for this position is between EUR 2,000 and EUR 3,400 per month (for a full-time role). The specific salary offered considers:
• the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role,
• the applicant’s own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialization, skills and experience.In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for additional rewards and benefits including an attractive performance-based bonus.
 We look forward to your application!
 We provide feedback to all candidates via email. If you have not heard back from us, please check your spam folder. #LI-Hybrid

 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. We cover both Property & Casualty and Life & Health. jobs.description:
Are you detail-oriented, analytically minded, and eager to build a meaningful career at the intersection of insurance operations and international business? At Swiss Re Corporate Solutions, we're looking for a curious and driven Underwriting Analyst to join our International Operations Business Services team in Toronto. This is your opportunity to work at the heart of a globally connected underwriting operation — where your contributions directly shape efficiency, accuracy, and client outcomes.
 About the Role
 As an Underwriting Analyst, you'll play a vital role in supporting our Property insurance underwriting operations, with a focus on International Programs. You'll be the operational backbone that keeps the underwriting process running smoothly — processing assignments with precision, coordinating across global teams, and providing critical administrative and technical support to Property Underwriters and Client Managers.
 Your work will have a direct and measurable impact on productivity, process efficiency, timeliness, profitability, and the overall accuracy of the underwriting process.
 Key Responsibilities

• Process and manage underwriting assignments accurately and within established turnaround standards, ensuring data integrity at every step

• Coordinate closely with underwriting teams, on-shore and off-shore support functions, and cross-functional partners including Products, Finance, and Claims

• Support international placement needs for Regions outside North America requiring local coverage, as well as North America teams placing coverage internationally

• Communicate professionally with Underwriters and Brokers via telephone, email, and in-person interactions, delivering consistently high-quality service

• Conduct preliminary deal analysis and prepare account data for review by Underwriters and Client Managers

• Review and interpret complex source documents from external customers, determining appropriate next steps and composing business correspondence as needed

• Collaborate on the development and maintenance of Standard Operating Procedures, system improvements, and process change testing and piloting

• Build subject matter expertise in International Business processes, tools, and systems — serving as a go-to resource and coach for colleagues

• Generate and verify predefined business reports, maintaining a high level of competency across complex systems and workflows

• Proactively problem-solve to meet and exceed client and broker expectations, while adhering to internal standards and controls

• Identify and recommend process and system improvement opportunities, contributing to ongoing operational reviews and task analyses

• Follow up with Underwriters and stakeholders on outstanding items and documentation to ensure timely resolution

• Participate in meetings, seminars, and training programs to stay current with international regulations and continuously develop your skills

• Contribute to special projects as assigned, supporting broader business and operational initiatives
 About the Team
 The International Operations Business Services team is a critical enabler of Swiss Re Corporate Solutions' global underwriting success. We sit at the intersection of local and international insurance placement, supporting regions across the globe who need to place local coverage, as well as North America teams placing coverage internationally.
 Our team thrives on high collaboration — working closely with underwriting, client management, finance, claims, and offshore support teams to ensure seamless, accurate, and timely operations. We are a team of subject matter experts who take pride in operational excellence, continuous improvement, and delivering top-notch service to our underwriters, brokers, and clients. If you enjoy working in a dynamic, globally connected environment where your contributions truly matter, you'll feel right at home here.
 About You
 You are a highly organized and detail-focused professional who thrives in a fast-paced, high-volume operational environment. You bring a quality-control mindset, a collaborative spirit, and the ability to navigate complexity across multiple systems, teams, and time zones. You take ownership of your work, communicate clearly, and are always looking for ways to improve the processes around you.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• 2–4 years of experience in insurance operations, underwriting support, or International Programs — with a solid understanding of property insurance workflows

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office tools including Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and SharePoint, with the ability to manage data and reporting across multiple platforms

• Demonstrated ability to interpret and follow structured operational processes, procedures, and controls — with experience managing multi-system workflows simultaneously

• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills , with the ability to engage effectively with globally distributed teams, brokers, underwriters, and stakeholders

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills , with the ability to identify discrepancies, assess impacts, and escalate issues appropriately
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Experience with audit readiness and documentation discipline , including data integrity and operational controls awareness

• Familiarity with multinational programs, local offices, and international regulatory frameworks

• Process improvement mindset — experience identifying and implementing operational efficiencies

• Ability to support system and process testing , including piloting operational change initiatives

• Multi-system coordination skills , including workflow dependency management across complex operational environments

• Comfort with adapting to evolving technologies and changing priorities in a dynamic global organization

• Strong customer service orientation with a track record of exceeding client and broker expectations
 The base salary hiring range for this existing position is CAD $75,000 - $92,000. The specific base salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.
 About Swiss Re Corporate Solutions
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer. We anticipate and manage risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime.

Swiss Re Corporate Solutions is the commercial insurance arm of the Swiss Re Group. We offer innovative insurance solutions to large and midsized multinational corporations from our approximately 50 locations worldwide. We help clients mitigate their risk exposure, whilst our industry-leading claims service provides them with additional peace of mind.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. Swiss Re Corporate Solutions embraces a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.
 We may use AI-powered tools to support the review and evaluation of applications for this position. These tools provide additional insights to our recruitment teams, but all hiring decisions are carefully reviewed and made by people. To learn more about how we use AI in recruitment and how we handle your personal data, please review our Data Privacy Statement before applying.

jobs.description:
Senior Digital Risk Advisor – Group Security & Technology Platforms
 Are you passionate about digital risk governance and making organizations more resilient? Join our dynamic team at Swiss Re, Bangalore, where you'll play a pivotal role in shaping how we identify, manage, and mitigate digital risks across our global operations. This is your opportunity to sit at the intersection of technology, risk management, and business strategy — helping to protect and strengthen one of the world's leading reinsurance companies while driving meaningful impact every day.

About the Role
 As a Senior Digital Risk Advisor, you'll serve as a trusted partner to our Group Security & Technology Platforms unit, ensuring that digital and technology risks are properly identified, assessed, and controlled. You'll help cultivate a robust risk culture while enabling innovation and business growth through smart, effective risk management practices. This is a high-visibility role where your expertise will directly influence how Swiss Re navigates the evolving digital risk landscape.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead risk assessments and control evaluations within the Group Security & Technology Platforms unit, ensuring comprehensive coverage of digital risk exposure

• Implement digital risk frameworks as a trusted advisor, ensuring IT threats and risks are clearly understood across the organization

• Design effective controls and embed them into operational procedures through close collaboration with technology teams

• Drive automation of control processes and spearhead continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen our overall risk posture

• Build operational transparency through continuous monitoring and assessment of controls against our defined risk appetite

• Coordinate audit activities and serve as the primary point of contact for Internal Audits, External Audits, and Compliance Risk Reviews

• Provide expert guidance on digital risk and control activities within the Group Security & Technology Platforms unit

• Promote risk awareness by staying current with evolving digital risk requirements and ensuring proper framework implementation across teams

• Foster innovation in risk management approaches and methodologies, bringing fresh thinking to how we manage and respond to digital risk

About the Team
 The Digital Risk Governance & Controls team is a cornerstone of Swiss Re's resilience strategy. We are dedicated to defining and managing risks related to digital topics, playing a crucial role in helping Swiss Re fulfill its mission of making the world more resilient. Our team ensures that digital risks are properly identified, assessed, and controlled at every level of the organization. We bring together deep technical expertise and sharp business acumen to deliver practical, forward-thinking risk management solutions — ones that protect the organization while actively enabling innovation and sustainable growth. We are a collaborative, curious, and driven group that values diverse perspectives and continuous learning.

About You
 You are a strategic thinker with a genuine passion for risk management and a collaborative, inclusive approach to problem-solving. You understand both the technical and business dimensions of digital risk and can communicate with clarity and confidence across all levels of the organization — from senior leadership to IT engineers. You are proactive, detail-oriented, and energized by continuous improvement. You thrive in dynamic environments and bring both rigor and creativity to the challenges of modern digital risk governance.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• Proven track record in IT risk and control-related roles such as IT Governance, IT Audit, or Digital Risk Management, with demonstrated ability to deliver results

• Strong knowledge of Risk Management Frameworks including COBIT, ISO 31000, COSO ERM, and/or NIST, and the ability to apply them pragmatically in a complex organization

• Industry experience in insurance, reinsurance, or banking, with a solid understanding of modern technology solutions and their associated risk profiles

• Fluency in spoken and written English, with strong communication skills and the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders at all levels

These are additional nice to haves:

• Professional qualifications such as CISA, CGEIT, CRISC, or equivalent certifications

• Experience with control automation and continuous monitoring techniques

• Background in application development or security engineering

• Demonstrated ability to build and maintain collaborative networks across IT domains

• Curiosity, proactivity, and confidence in decision-making at pace, with a solutions-first mindset

Our company has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office at least three days per week.
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. We cover both Property & Casualty and Life & Health. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients.  Are you passionate about digital risk governance and making organizations more resilient? Join our dynamic team at Swiss Re, Bangalore, where you'll play a pivotal role in shaping how we identify, manage, and mitigate digital risks across our global operations. This is your opportunity to sit at the intersection of technology, risk management, and business strategy — helping to protect and strengthen one of the world's leading reinsurance companies while driving meaningful impact every day.

About the Role
 As a Senior Digital Risk Advisor, you'll serve as a trusted partner to our Group Security & Technology Platforms unit, ensuring that digital and technology risks are properly identified, assessed, and controlled. You'll help cultivate a robust risk culture while enabling innovation and business growth through smart, effective risk management practices. This is a high-visibility role where your expertise will directly influence how Swiss Re navigates the evolving digital risk landscape.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead risk assessments and control evaluations within the Group Security & Technology Platforms unit, ensuring comprehensive coverage of digital risk exposure

• Implement digital risk frameworks as a trusted advisor, ensuring IT threats and risks are clearly understood across the organization

• Design effective controls and embed them into operational procedures through close collaboration with technology teams

• Drive automation of control processes and spearhead continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen our overall risk posture

• Build operational transparency through continuous monitoring and assessment of controls against our defined risk appetite

• Coordinate audit activities and serve as the primary point of contact for Internal Audits, External Audits, and Compliance Risk Reviews

• Provide expert guidance on digital risk and control activities within the Group Security & Technology Platforms unit

• Promote risk awareness by staying current with evolving digital risk requirements and ensuring proper framework implementation across teams

• Foster innovation in risk management approaches and methodologies, bringing fresh thinking to how we manage and respond to digital risk

About the Team
 The Digital Risk Governance & Controls team is a cornerstone of Swiss Re's resilience strategy. We are dedicated to defining and managing risks related to digital topics, playing a crucial role in helping Swiss Re fulfill its mission of making the world more resilient. We bring together deep technical expertise and sharp business acumen to deliver practical, forward-thinking risk management solutions — ones that protect the organization while actively enabling innovation and sustainable growth. We are a collaborative, curious, and driven group that values diverse perspectives and continuous learning.

 You are a strategic thinker with a genuine passion for risk management and a collaborative, inclusive approach to problem-solving. You understand both the technical and business dimensions of digital risk and can communicate with clarity and confidence across all levels of the organization — from senior leadership to IT engineers. You are proactive, detail-oriented, and energized by continuous improvement. • Industry experience in insurance, reinsurance, or banking, with a solid understanding of modern technology solutions and their associated risk profiles

jobs.title: Modelling Lead Americas
jobs.description:
Are you a seasoned leader with deep expertise in Life & Health valuation and a passion for building future-ready modelling solutions? If you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and love uniting diverse teams around a shared purpose, this could be the role for you!

About the Role
 As the Modelling Lead Americas, you will be at the heart of Swiss Re's actuarial and financial modelling capabilities, driving the development, maintenance, and execution of critical valuation models. Your remit spans a broad and exciting geographic scope — covering Life & Health products across the US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability products in Australia — making this a truly global leadership opportunity. You will play a pivotal role in shaping the strategic direction of modelling across these regions, ensuring our models are robust, forward-looking, and aligned with evolving regulatory and reporting standards. This is a rare opportunity to make a lasting impact at the intersection of technical excellence and strategic leadership.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead and inspire a diverse, high-performing modelling team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement

• Develop, maintain, and run Life & Health valuation models across US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability models for Australia , ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with business objectives

• Drive financial reporting excellence across US Statutory, IFRS and local statutory reporting frameworks, ensuring compliance and consistency across all regions

• Design and implement future-ready modelling solutions , anticipating business needs and regulatory changes across multiple jurisdictions

• Manage strategic relationships with external modelling and technology vendors , ensuring solutions meet business needs, deliver value, and support the long-term evolution of the modelling ecosystem

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Swiss Re's actuarial, finance, and technology teams to deliver integrated, end-to-end modelling capabilities

• Manage model governance, validation, and documentation standards, ensuring models are robust, accurate, fit for purpose, and supported by transparent, auditable processes.

• Navigate ambiguity and complexity with confidence, providing clear direction and pragmatic solutions in a rapidly evolving, multi-regional landscape

• Engage senior stakeholders , communicating complex modelling concepts and results in a clear, compelling, and accessible manner

• Mentor and develop team members , building technical depth and leadership capability across the modelling function

About the Team
 The Modelling Centre of Excellence (MCoE) Americas is a dynamic and collaborative team dedicated to developing, maintaining, and running critical valuation models representing more than half of Swiss Re's Life & Health exposure globally. The team's scope spans Life & Health products across the US, Canada, and Latin America , as well as disability products in Australia , reflecting the breadth and diversity of Swiss Re's reinsurance portfolio. The team plays a critical role in supporting Swiss Re's financial reporting and strategic decision-making, combining deep technical expertise with a forward-thinking approach to modelling innovation.

About You
 You are a seasoned valuation and modelling professional and an inspiring leader who brings both deep technical expertise and a strategic mindset to everything you do. You are resilient, calm under pressure, and skilled at navigating complexity and ambiguity across diverse geographies and product lines. You have a natural ability to unite diverse teams around shared goals, and you are passionate about designing solutions that are not just fit for today, but ready for tomorrow.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• Expert knowledge of Life & Health products , including valuation methodologies and financial reporting frameworks across US, Canada, Latin America, and Australia

• Deep expertise in L&H Valuation and Financial Reporting , with hands-on experience in both US Statutory and IFRS standards

• Strong technical understanding of actuarial and finance systems , including proficiency with Moody's AXIS modelling platform

• Strong leadership experience, with the ability to develop high-performing, geographically diverse teams and unite cross-functional stakeholders around shared objectives.
 These are additional nice to haves:

• Resilience and composure under pressure , with the ability to deliver high-quality outcomes in fast-moving, high-stakes environments

• Skilled in managing ambiguity and resolving conflicts , bringing clarity and direction when challenges arise

• Strategic mindset , with demonstrated ability to design and implement future-ready, scalable solutions

• Experience working in a global or matrixed organization , navigating complex stakeholder landscapes across geographies

Our company uses a hybrid work model requiring at least three days in the office each week, with the option to work onsite full-time if preferred. This position is not eligible for full-time telework or relocation assistance.

The base salary hiring range for this new position located in Toronto is CAD $180,000 to $230,000. The specific base salary offered for this or any given role will take into account a number of factors including but not limited to job location, scope of role, qualifications, complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent, experience, education, and employer budget. At Swiss Re, we take a "total compensation approach" when making compensation decisions. This means that we consider all components of compensation in their totality (such as base pay, short-and long-term incentives, and benefits offered), in setting individual compensation.

jobs.description:
As a AI Engineering Lead, you own high‑impact data, AI and analytics solutions for the Property & Casualty (P&C) domain, working with modern big‑data technologies and Ai techniques to turn complex data that support business decisions. You’ll be also acting as a technical lead and mentor, shaping best practices and supporting other engineers’ growth as their line manager.
 Here's a taste of what you could be doing:

• Lead and mentor a team of engineers, setting clear technical standards and fostering a culture of engineering excellence, learning, and ownership

• Act as a hands-on technical authority for AI systems, with the ability to review, challenge, and contribute to architecture, code, and implementation decisions

• Drive the design and implementation of scalable AI and ML platforms, including MLOps, data pipelines, and cloud-native infrastructure

• Ensure solutions are technically sound, deliver business value, and can be operated reliably at scale

• Oversee the end-to-end delivery lifecycle of the products, from experimentation and prototyping through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement

• Guide teams in applying modern AI techniques, including Generative AI, while ensuring robustness, security, explainability, and compliance
 The best part? We are a highly skilled team working on global initiatives across Swiss Re. Our passion for learning connects us: we actively invest in upskilling, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement, and we expect our leaders to role-model this mindset.
 About you
 In order to be successful in the role, you bring:

• A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience

• Extensive experience designing, building, and operating production-grade systems

• Strong proficiency in Python (or similar languages) and a deep understanding of good software engineering principles

• Solid hands-on knowledge of MLOps practices, including CI/CD for ML, model monitoring, versioning, and lifecycle management

• Deep understanding of cloud-native architectures, distributed systems, and large-scale data processing

• Proven experience in technical leadership roles, including mentoring engineers and guiding complex technical decisions
 It is a strong plus if you also have:

• Experience leading AI or data engineering teams in a large organization

• Experience with Generative AI, NLP, or other advanced AI techniques applied in real-world products
 Even if you do not meet every requirement, we welcome applications from candidates who are eager to grow into the role and assume significant technical and leadership responsibilities.
 Thank you for taking the time to read our job advertisement. We look forward to getting to know you.
 For Slovakia the base salary range for this position is between EUR 3,200 and EUR 5,300 per month (for a full-time role). The specific salary offered considers:​

• the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role, ​

• the applicant’s own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialisation, skills and experience.​
 In addition to your base salary, Swiss Re offers an attractive performance-based variable compensation component, designed to recognise your achievements. Further you will enjoy a variety of global and location specific benefits.​

jobs.title: Finance Reporting Manager
jobs.description:
We're seeking a dynamic finance reporting leader who can drive excellence in financial reporting while building strong stakeholder relationships and leading a team to success!
 About the Role
 This management position oversees financial reporting and analysis of assigned legal entities in the U.S. You'll lead a team to deliver valuable insights to other finance and business functions through expert and timely information while driving continuous improvement initiatives.
 Key Responsibilities

• Lead and develop a team responsible for high-quality US Statutory financial reporting for assigned legal entities, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to regulatory and internal governance requirements

• Direct and oversee comprehensive financial and variance analysis, clearly communicating results and key drivers to senior finance and business stakeholders

• Establish and maintain robust internal control activities within the reporting process, identifying issues and implementing effective remediation strategies

• Drive innovation by identifying opportunities for process improvement, including automation and standardization, and leading implementation efforts

• Build and nurture strategic relationships with internal partners and external stakeholders to support reporting and analytical objectives

• Mentor and coach team members to develop their technical and soft skills, fostering a culture of continuous learning and growth
 About the Team
 The Americas Carrier Management Team is constantly developing and strengthening our capabilities to provide insightful and meaningful reporting to our decision makers. You will join a highly motivated and dynamic team within an interesting and complex environment and will get the opportunity to build up and further enhance reporting, consolidation & analytical capabilities.
 About You
 You're a strategic thinker with excellent leadership abilities who thrives on developing both processes and people. Your strong communication skills and business acumen enable you to translate complex financial information into actionable insights for stakeholders at all levels. You're passionate about fostering an inclusive team environment while driving operational excellence.
 We are looking for candidates who meet these requirements:

• 10+ years of experience in the life insurance industry or audit experience, including team leadership responsibilities

• Four-year Accounting for Finance degree; CPA certification or equivalent preferable

• Comprehensive knowledge of U.S. Statutory accounting and reporting standards for life insurance companies

jobs.title: Reinsurance Contracts Expert
jobs.description:
Head of P&C Reinsurance Contracts, Asia Pacific is seeking a regional Reinsurance contract wordings counsel / expert to join our team supporting Swiss Re's property and casualty ("P&C") reinsurance business in the Asia Pacific region. Primary responsibilities include drafting and review of (re)insurance contract wordings, advising on contract related matters, and engaging with internal and, at times, external clients to negotiate and finalize the terms of reinsurance contracts, as well as supporting the Head of P&C Reinsurance Contracts to manage contract risks in reinsurance portfolio. This position will be based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

About the team
 P&C Contracts is part of Underwriting Excellence in Property & Casualty Reinsurance . It is responsible for ensuring Swiss Re (re)insurance agreements comply with underwriting and contracts standards.
 In P&C Contracts, you will join a highly engaged global team of approximately 40 legal / claims / underwriting experts and specialists who support all Lines of Property, Casualty, and Specialty business. Primary responsibilities of our Contracts Function include drafting and review of (re)insurance wordings, advising on contract related matters and engaging with internal and external clients to negotiate and finalize the terms of reinsurance contracts as well as the further development of our tool landscape and wording analytics.

About the role
 Core responsibilities of the Reinsurance Contracts Expert / Counsel are:

• Independently draft and critique (re)insurance contracts, binders, slips, endorsements and related documents to align written agreements with business intent and corporate requirement.

• Perform portfolio analysis and provide insights on trends related to contract risks, in reliance on Swiss Re contracts systems and database.

• Align reinsurance contracts with applicable law, regulations and internal requirements.

• Coordinate, communicate and participate in development of corporate policies on contract related matters.

• Support functional development of contract management and analytical systems;

• Collaborate with Client Managers and Underwriters in contract negotiations, including discussions with external clients and brokers.

• Act as expert technical advisor, providing guidance to various corporate functions regarding contract formation / interpretation, implications of particular contract language and best practices.

• Develop training materials and deliver internal, external or public training on contract related matters; drive thought leadership on contract certainty.

• Maintain strong governance risk and control standards with respect to contract wordings and processes.

About You
 The successful candidate will be expected to develop a thorough understanding of relevant law, regulations and market practices in the Asia Pacific region and apply these to (re)insurance agreements. Participation in Global projects / initiatives through co-working with team mates from the US and EMEA Regions is expected. They will also require strong analytical abilities, experience in business negotiations, and excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to engage confidently and in an impactful manner with internal stakeholders and clients. We are seeking a candidate with an innovative, pragmatic and results-oriented mindset, who possesses the ability to work independently with a sense of personal responsibility and accountability, while also building cooperative relationships with internal and external partners, to enable cross-functional team decision making in alignment with Swiss Re business strategy. The Contracts Expert / Counsel should be available for business travel roughly two weeks each year.
 Requirements for the Reinsurance Contracts Expert / Counsel position include:

• Degree holder in business, finance, insurance, law or a related field; preferably with professional insurance designation (e.g. ACII or equivalent); legal background / qualification in common / English law an advantage;

• 5 or more years of (re)insurance industry experience (re)insurance claims, underwriting, coverage counsel, legal or product role;

• Solid understanding of P&C (re)insurance policy wordings, coverage, product, and business processes;

• Good skill and confidence in commercial / (re)insurance coverage agreement drafting;

• External customer servicing, management, or advising experience an advantage;

• Exposure to a multi-cultural work and / or client servicing environment; and

• High level fluency in Chinese and English, including business terminology. Additional fluency in Mandarin is a plus;

• Effective computer and Information Technology literacy.
 About Swiss Re
 Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.

This position will be based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

About the team
 P&C Contracts is part of Underwriting Excellence in Property & Casualty Reinsurance . It is responsible for ensuring Swiss Re (re)insurance agreements comply with underwriting and contracts standards.
 In P&C Contracts, you will join a highly engaged global team of approximately 40 legal / claims / underwriting experts and specialists who support all Lines of Property, Casualty, and Specialty business. Primary responsibilities of our Contracts Function include drafting and review of (re)insurance wordings, advising on contract related matters and engaging with internal and external clients to negotiate and finalize the terms of reinsurance contracts as well as the further development of our tool landscape and wording analytics.

About the role
 Core responsibilities of the Reinsurance Contracts Expert / Counsel are:

• Independently draft and critique (re)insurance contracts, binders, slips, endorsements and related documents to align written agreements with business intent and corporate requirement.

• Perform portfolio analysis and provide insights on trends related to contract risks, in reliance on Swiss Re contracts systems and database.

• Align reinsurance contracts with applicable law, regulations and internal requirements.

• Coordinate, communicate and participate in development of corporate policies on contract related matters.

• Support functional development of contract management and analytical systems;

• Collaborate with Client Managers and Underwriters in contract negotiations, including discussions with external clients and brokers.

• Act as expert technical advisor, providing guidance to various corporate functions regarding contract formation / interpretation, implications of particular contract language and best practices.

• Develop training materials and deliver internal, external or public training on contract related matters; drive thought leadership on contract certainty.

• Maintain strong governance risk and control standards with respect to contract wordings and processes.

About You
 The successful candidate will be expected to develop a thorough understanding of relevant law, regulations and market practices in the Asia Pacific region and apply these to (re)insurance agreements. Participation in Global projects / initiatives through co-working with team mates from the US and EMEA Regions is expected. They will also require strong analytical abilities, experience in business negotiations, and excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to engage confidently and in an impactful manner with internal stakeholders and clients. We are seeking a candidate with an innovative, pragmatic and results-oriented mindset, who possesses the ability to work independently with a sense of personal responsibility and accountability, while also building cooperative relationships with internal and external partners, to enable cross-functional team decision making in alignment with Swiss Re business strategy. The Contracts Expert / Counsel should be available for business travel roughly two weeks each year.
 Requirements for the Reinsurance Contracts Expert / Counsel position include:

• Degree holder in business, finance, insurance, law or a related field; preferably with professional insurance designation (e.g. ACII or equivalent); legal background / qualification in common / English law an advantage;

• 5 or more years of (re)insurance industry experience (re)insurance claims, underwriting, coverage counsel, legal or product role;

• Solid understanding of P&C (re)insurance policy wordings, coverage, product, and business processes;

• Good skill and confidence in commercial / (re)insurance coverage agreement drafting;

• External customer servicing, management, or advising experience an advantage;

• Exposure to a multi-cultural work and / or client servicing environment; and

• High level fluency in Chinese and English, including business terminology. Additional fluency in Mandarin is a plus;

• Effective computer and Information Technology literacy.

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about Life & Health Reinsurance and the full value chain? Do you enjoy working at the intersection of business, risk, and governance - shaping how decisions are made and risks are managed?
 We are looking for a driven and forward-thinking professional to join our global Operational Resilience & Governance L&H Re team. This role offers a unique opportunity to act as a trusted advisor and challenger to stakeholders at all levels, influencing how risk and governance are embedded across the business.
 You will operate at the heart of the organization, partnering with business leaders across regions and functions to strengthen risk transparency, enhance control effectiveness, and drive forward-looking governance practices.

About the Role

• Act as a trusted advisor to business leaders, shaping and challenging how operational, compliance, and regulatory risks are managed across the L&H Re value chain

• Continuously enhance the risk and control framework, ensuring it remains fit for purpose in a dynamic and evolving environment

• Identify key risk and control gaps, drive targeted improvements, and promote a strong, proactive risk culture across teams

• Provide expert guidance on operational risk and governance topics, including events, issues, and audits, with a focus on practical and sustainable solutions

• Lead or contribute to high-impact governance initiatives, collaborating with global assurance functions to strengthen the overall control environment

• Leverage process mapping, digital tools and data analytics to increase transparency, enable better decision-making, and anticipate emerging risks
 About the Team
 The Operational Resilience & Governance team sits within Business Operations L&H Re. We are a diverse, global team with a clear mandate: to align governance, regulatory compliance, risk management, and internal controls into a cohesive and forward-looking framework.
 We work closely with the business to not only safeguard today’s operations, but to anticipate and prepare for future challenges, making us a key enabler of sustainable performance.

About You

• 7+ years of experience in Insurance or Reinsurance, with a strong understanding of L&H business (Swiss Re experience is a plus)

• Solid expertise in the three lines of defence model and its practical application

• Proven ability to navigate complexity, connect the dots, and translate insights into action

• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively and influence senior audiences

• A high level of ownership, with a track record of delivering outcomes and driving change initiatives

• Outstanding teammate with strong communication and interpersonal skills

• Advanced ability to leverage AI and digital tools to enhance analysis, improve efficiency, and support better risk insights and decision-making

• University degree or equivalent professional experience

• Fluent in English; additional languages are a plus
 For Slovakia the base salary range for this position is between EUR 3100 and EUR 5100 per month (for a full-time role). The specific salary offered considers:​
 • the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role, ​
 • the applicant’s own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialisation, skills and experience.​
 In addition to your base salary, Swiss Re offers an attractive performance-based variable compensation component, designed to recognise your achievements. Further you will enjoy a variety of global and location specific benefits.​
 Eligibility may vary depending on the terms of Swiss Re policies and your employment contract.
 We provide feedback to all candidates via email. If you have not heard back from us, please check your spam folder. #LI- Hybrid

• Experience in workflow orchestration and scheduling tools and frameworks

• Understanding of key ITIL processes , including incident, problem, and release management
